papers.title: A Diffusion-Based Generative Framework for Synthetic Arrhythmia ECG Signals
papers.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare Systems
papers.model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM, 1D U-Net denoiser, class encoder + attention conditioning) — conceptual framework
papers.datasets: proposed for MIT-BIH, PTB-XL, MIMIC-ECG (no experiments run)
papers.loss_functions: simplified DDPM noise-prediction MSE; downstream classifier consistency regularization via KL divergence between outputs on real vs synthetic same-class samples
papers.eval_metrics: Fréchet distance on pretrained ECG encoder embeddings; MMD (RBF); SNR (>20 dB criterion); QRS duration, QTc, RR variability, ST deviation distribution matching via KS test (p>0.05); blinded cardiologist Turing test (100 real/100 synthetic, ~50% target); class-conditional controllability audits; AUROC, F1, sensitivity at fixed specificity (TSTR/augmentation); synthetic-vs-real generalization gap (<5 pp); paired bootstrap CIs (10,000); membership inference; nearest-neighbour distance
papers.embedding_extractor: pretrained ECG encoder (unspecified)
papers.notes: Explicitly 'no experimental results' — a theoretical blueprint. Useful as a checklist mapping validation domains to metrics and success thresholds (Table 2). Claims diffusion inherently resists membership inference (unverified). Notes sampling cost 30-60 s per 10 s 12-lead ECG at T=1000.
papers.takeaway: Its domain->metric->threshold table (FD/MMD, KS on clinical intervals, expert Turing, TSTR gap, MIA/NN privacy) is a good template for ECGEN-Eval report sections.

papers.title: A Generative Methodology for PPG to ECG Reconstruction Based on Dual-Critic Approach
papers.model_family: GAN (dual-critic WGAN-GP, LSTM+multi-head-attention generator; time-domain and DWT-domain critics)
papers.datasets: BIDMC (53 ICU patients), ECG lead II
papers.loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss from time-domain critic (weighted alpha=10) + Wasserstein loss from DWT-domain critic + gradient penalty (lambda=10) on both critics
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE (normalized); MAE of heart rate (MAE_HR); PRD
papers.notes: Paired PPG->ECG; RMSE 0.134, MAE_HR 3.75, PRD 6.064 vs CardioGAN. Wavelet-domain critic is a frequency-aware adversarial loss. Inference timing on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin reported. Small dataset (53 patients), 80/20 split (subject independence unclear).
papers.takeaway: Heart-rate MAE between paired real/generated ECG is a cheap clinical check; wavelet-domain comparison could complement PSD.

papers.title: A GENERATIVE MODEL FOR DEEP FAKE AUGMENTATION OF PHONOCARDIOGRAM AND ELECTROCARDIOGRAM SIGNALS USING LSGAN AND CYCLE GAN
papers.venue: Informatyka Automatyka Pomiary w Gospodarce i Ochronie Środowiska
papers.model_family: GAN (LSGAN; CycleGAN)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia; PTB Diagnostic (stated); PCG: PASCAL Heart Sound Challenge, PhysioNet CinC 2016, Michigan Heart Sound and Murmur Library
papers.loss_functions: Least-squares adversarial loss (LSGAN); CycleGAN adversarial + cycle-consistency loss
papers.eval_metrics: MSE; SSIM; PSNR (defined, not tabulated); cross-correlation coefficient (defined); VGG-16 arrhythmia classification accuracy, precision, recall, F1
papers.notes: CycleGAN ECG: MSE 0.0651, SSIM 0.9823; classifier F1 0.9035. Reported numbers inconsistent between abstract/table and conclusion (F1 90.35% vs 97.22%). Image metrics (SSIM, PSNR) applied to 1-D signals; pairing protocol for MSE/SSIM not described.
papers.takeaway: Weak evaluation example: image metrics on 1-D signals without stated pairing; ECGEN-Eval should state pairing (nearest neighbour) explicitly.

papers.title: A peak-oriented diffusion model for high-fidelity electrocardiogram reconstruction from photoplethysmogram: development and usability study
authors: Cho HM, Han S, Seong JK, Youn I.
papers.model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM, 1-D U-Net with self-attention + MLP R-peak predictor on bottleneck)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III Waveform Matched Subset (+ MIMIC-III Clinical DB for CVD/AF labels); WESAD; PPG-DaLiA (cross-dataset)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction MSE (λ1=1) + L2 R-peak position prediction loss (λ2=1); cosine schedule, T=300
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; Fréchet distance (FD); duration RMSE of P-wave, PR, QRS, QT, T-wave (ms, DWT delineation); peak timing RMSE for P/Q/R/S/T peaks; peak amplitude RMSE; AF detection accuracy/precision/recall/F1 (ResNet-50 trained on real ECG only, tested on reconstructed); HR estimation Bland-Altman mean difference; KS, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney with Bonferroni for noise robustness
papers.notes: Argues RMSE/FD ignore short PQRST components and adds per-wave duration/peak-timing RMSE. Results: RMSE 0.220, FD 6.456, AF F1 0.925, HR bias -0.077 bpm; R-peak timing RMSE 19.7 ms. Robustness tested with white noise and motion artifacts; ~60M segments from 5,888 patients.
papers.takeaway: Per-fiducial timing/amplitude RMSE (P/Q/R/S/T) and interval-duration errors are a cheap clinically-anchored complement to RMSE/FD for paired tasks.

papers.title: A performance analysis of convolutional autoencoder modified WaveGAN architectures for realistic 12 lead electrocardiogram synthesis
papers.model_family: GAN (WaveGAN/WGAN-style with convolutional-autoencoder feature extractor; CAE-WaveGAN)
papers.datasets: CODE-15% (training/ablation); PTB-XL (visual comparison only)
papers.signal_length_s: ~10 (4096 samples, 7 s and 10 s records zero-padded)
papers.loss_functions: CAE reconstruction loss (MSE or BCE); Wasserstein adversarial loss for discriminator/generator (WGAN-style critic loss)
papers.eval_metrics: PSNR; SSIM; Morphology Similarity (MorphSim); Spectral Similarity (SpecSim); standard deviation of generator training/validation loss (stability); epoch time
papers.notes: PSNR reported ~4 dB and SSIM 0.18, i.e. very low absolute values; 'improvement' framed as relative %. Loss-std used as stability metric. Pitfall: threshold-based quality filtering (MorphSim>=0.50, SpecSim>=0.80, SSIM threshold) before showing samples = cherry-picking. No distribution, utility or privacy metrics.
papers.takeaway: MorphSim/SpecSim are cheap per-sample sanity metrics, but avoid post-hoc quality filtering and absolute PSNR/SSIM on unpaired generations.

papers.title: A Physics-Aware Diffusion Framework for Robust ECG Synthesis Using Mesoscopic Lattice Boltzmann Constraints
papers.model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM with Lattice-Boltzmann physics encoder, 'PhysDiff-LBM')
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III Waveform DB; VitalDB (OOD generalization); MIMIC PERform AF (downstream AF classification); PhysioNet Challenge 2015 (5-class arrhythmia downstream)
papers.loss_functions: Weighted sum: DDPM noise-prediction MSE (L_diff) + BCE topology loss vs ground-truth QRS mask (L_reg) + hemodynamic physics-consistency loss (L2 between temporal derivative of Tweedie-estimated x0 and LBM momentum flux, L_phys)
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; HR-MAE (heart rate via Pan-Tompkins); Fréchet Distance on raw signal windows; downstream AF / arrhythmia classification Accuracy, Precision, Recall/Sensitivity, Specificity, F1, AUC with 95% bootstrap CIs, paired permutation and DeLong tests
papers.notes: FD defined as Wasserstein-2 between Gaussian fits of raw 1-D windows (no embedding). Downstream utility = classifier on generated vs real ECG vs raw PPG; Gen ECG close to Real ECG. Bootstrap CIs and DeLong tests are good statistical practice.
papers.takeaway: HR-MAE (Pan-Tompkins HR error) and downstream classifier comparison with bootstrap CIs/DeLong tests are cheap, clinically meaningful additions.

papers.title: A Usable GAN-Based Tool for Synthetic ECG Generation in Cardiac Amyloidosis Research
papers.model_family: GAN (vanilla GAN, BiLSTM generator/discriminator, class-specific)
papers.task: class-cond (beat augmentation; tool for cardiac amyloidosis)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (Kaggle-style 187-sample beat CSV); planned CA cohorts
papers.loss_functions: standard BCE adversarial loss (D: real/fake BCE; G: non-saturating BCE)
papers.eval_metrics: Planned only: DTW; discrete Fréchet distance; Euclidean distance; nearest-synthetic-neighbour distance (median/IQR); productivity rate (fraction of real beats within 95th-pct real-real distance of a synthetic beat); KS test + Cohen's d on QRS duration, R amplitude, QRS area, ST level, T amplitude; Hotelling T²; energy distance; MMD on embeddings; accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1, AUROC, AUPRC; Brier score; ECE; decision-curve analysis; silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, ARI, bootstrap Jaccard cluster stability
papers.embedding_extractor: penultimate layer of AI-ECG classifier or autoencoder (planned)
papers.notes: No quantitative results; evaluation protocol is planned. Interesting ideas: 'productivity rate' coverage metric, calibration (Brier/ECE) of augmented classifiers, cluster-stability of augmented data.
papers.takeaway: Adopt 'productivity rate' (coverage of real samples within real-real 95th-percentile radius) and KS+Cohen's d per clinical feature.

papers.title: ABC-GAN: An Attention-Based Conditional GAN with DTW Loss for ECG Signal Generation to Address Class Imbalance
papers.venue: Journal of Information Systems and Telecommunication (JIST)
papers.model_family: GAN (ABC-GAN: conditional WGAN-GP with attention-based CNN generator)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (7 classes: P, A, L, N, R, f, j)
papers.signal_length_s: single heartbeat (75% of RR interval before/after R-peak)
papers.loss_functions: Critic: Wasserstein loss + gradient penalty; Generator: -E[critic(fake,label)] + lambda_dtw * DTW loss (sum of DTW between batch real[i] and fake[i]); ablations with MSE and KL-divergence terms instead of DTW
papers.eval_metrics: DTW (to nearest real sample, to class cluster center); MSE; KL divergence of amplitude histograms; downstream 1D-ResNet34 Precision, Recall, Accuracy, F1-score (train real+synthetic, test real)
papers.notes: DTW-threshold (3) post-hoc filtering of generated beats; up to 54% outliers for class P. DTW loss pairs unpaired batch real/fake samples. Augmented accuracy 0.95 vs 0.89 (WGAN-GP), 0.92 (MSE), 0.89 (KL). Medoid-by-DTW class template for evaluation.
papers.takeaway: Per-class DTW-to-nearest-real outlier rate is a useful plausibility/rejection metric; report per-class.

papers.title: AI based ECG data recovery and cardiovascular diseases classification (CEDRC-network)
authors: Khan MR, Haider ZM, Hussain J, Khan MA, Abdullah S.
papers.model_family: VAE (beta-VAE) vs Temporal Fusion Transformer, plus Transformer-based convolutional denoising AE (TCDAE)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (Diagnostic ECG Matched Subset), 2426 patients
papers.loss_functions: TCDAE: frequency-weighted Huber + cosine similarity loss; VAE: reconstruction + beta*KL; TFT: quantile loss over leads and horizons (observed-mask indicator); classifiers: cross-entropy
papers.eval_metrics: MAE; MSE; RMSE; NRMSE; Pearson correlation and energy difference (%) per lead (denoising); PSD comparison; downstream ML classification accuracy, F1 (AF, sinus bradycardia, tachycardia, sinus rhythm) at 10/30/50% missing; bootstrap (1000) accuracy SD; McNemar's test
papers.notes: TFT MAE 0.015, RMSE 0.0132 vs VAE MAE 0.075, RMSE 0.107; patient-level split; McNemar test for paired classifier comparison; bootstrap CIs. Evaluation is reconstruction-oriented, not generative distribution matching.
papers.takeaway: Bootstrap CIs and McNemar's paired test are good statistical practice for utility comparisons in ECGEN-Eval reports.

papers.title: AI modeling photoplethysmography to electrocardiography useful for predicting cardiovascular disease
papers.model_family: AR-Transformer (TimeVQVAE-style: STFT dual-band LF/HF VQ-VAE + bidirectional masked-token Transformers, PPG-conditioned via CLIP-style contrastive PPG encoder); Hybrid
papers.datasets: PulseDB-MIMIC; PulseDB-VitalDB; MESA (pretraining); MIMIC-AF subset; private BBX smart-ring PPG-AF set; PPG-DaLiA; WESAD
papers.loss_functions: Stage 0: symmetric InfoNCE/CLIP contrastive loss (PPG-ECG, τ=0.05) + MAE reconstruction pretraining; Stage 1: VQ codebook + β-commitment loss + L2 reconstruction (ISTFT) for LF and HF; Stage 2: masked-token negative log-likelihood (cross-entropy) for LF/HF priors
papers.eval_metrics: FID (on ROCKET features); Fréchet Distance on raw signals (FD); Marginal Distribution Difference (MDD); Autocorrelation Difference (ACD); Skewness Difference (SD); Kurtosis Difference (KD); MAE; MSE; PSNR; SSIM; downstream CVD screening AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, PPV, NPV, F1, kappa (DeLong, McNemar, bootstrap)
papers.embedding_extractor: ROCKET random-convolution features for FID
papers.notes: Uses TSGBench-style stats (MDD, ACD, SD, KD) alongside FID/FD/PSNR/SSIM; baselines RDDM, WGAN, RecQRS. ACD 0.367 vs 31.0 second-best; FID 0.001 vs 0.008. Primary aim is CVD prediction from PPG; generation is for interpretability.
papers.takeaway: Add cheap time-series distribution stats (marginal-distribution, autocorrelation, skewness, kurtosis differences) and a ROCKET-feature FID variant.

papers.title: AI-based 3-Lead to 12-Lead ECG Reconstruction: Towards Smartphone-based Public Healthcare
papers.model_family: GAN (1D Pix2Pix conditional GAN, UNet generator, PatchGAN-style 1D interval discriminator); baselines LSTM, LSTM-UNet
papers.datasets: Train: SPH (Shaoxing), CPSC2018, Georgia, INCART; Test: PTB, PTB-XL
papers.signal_length_s: PTB-XL ~5 s records (as stated); PTB 30 s; sliding windows
papers.loss_functions: not explicitly reported (1D Pix2Pix conditional adversarial objective implied)
papers.eval_metrics: coefficient of determination R2; Pearson correlation coefficient rx; per-lead and per-diagnostic-subgroup (HC, BB, HY, MI, VA, ND) analysis
papers.notes: Public (cross-patient) vs personalized setting comparison. R2 84.8%/rx 93.2% on PTB-XL vs LSTM-UNet 74.6%/86.0%. Leads V4-V6 hardest. Pitfall: early stopping on highest R2 on the test dataset. R2 formula as printed is non-standard.
papers.takeaway: Report reconstruction metrics per lead and per diagnostic subgroup; R2 + Pearson are standard paired metrics for lead reconstruction.

papers.title: Are AI-generated electrocardiograms clinically accurate? Benchmarking accuracy of AI-generated ECGs: a multiplatform performance study of public LLMs
papers.model_family: EvalOnly (public text-to-image/LLM platforms: Bard, Bing Image Creator, DALL-E)
papers.task: evaluation (text-cond ECG image generation by general-purpose AI)
papers.datasets: 113 AI-generated ECG images (10 rhythms x 3 platforms x 4, after exclusions)
papers.loss_functions: not applicable
papers.eval_metrics: Blinded expert rhythm diagnosis by 3 physicians incl. cardiologist with adjudication; accuracy = agreement with prompted rhythm; proportion uninterpretable
papers.notes: Conference abstract. Only 32.7% of 113 ECGs matched intended rhythm; 25.1% uninterpretable. Bard 84.5% correct but mostly retrieved existing online images (memorisation/retrieval pitfall). AFL 58.3%, AF 50% best.
papers.takeaway: Label-consistency (does generated ECG match prompted class?) via expert or classifier, plus retrieval/memorisation check, is essential for conditional generators.

papers.title: Bayesian ECG reconstruction using denoising diffusion generative models
papers.model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDGM/DDPM, EDM-like U-Net; 'ECGDiff') used as Bayesian prior via MCGdiff SMC posterior sampling
papers.task: class-cond (healthy beat conditioned on age, sex, RR); imputation (missing-lead reconstruction); denoising; anomaly detection
papers.datasets: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 (43,101 records; 28,167 patients normal beats, 468 MI patients)
papers.signal_length_s: 0.704 (single beat, R-192 ms to R+512 ms; 176 samples)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM denoising objective (equivalent to KL between inference and backward processes); no adversarial loss
papers.eval_metrics: Earth Mover's Distance (EMD, L2 transport cost on ECG concatenated with age/sex/RR) generated vs test/train; out-of-distribution uncertainty via random-network-distillation-style ResNet pairs (B=10); rescaled Mahalanobis distance of posterior; R² score for missing-lead reconstruction vs Dower matrix; R² for QT-vs-RR vs Bazett/Fridericia/Framingham; ROC for MI detection
papers.embedding_extractor: randomly initialised + trained ResNet pair (RND-style uncertainty), not a pretrained classifier
papers.notes: Proposes two 'novel' metrics: global EMD (with conditioning features in transport cost; compared gen-vs-test against test-vs-train baseline) and per-sample out-of-support uncertainty. Missing-lead R² 0.98-0.99 vs Dower 0.71-0.87. Amplitude-normalised beats, so amplitude fidelity is not evaluated.
papers.takeaway: Adopt EMD with real-vs-real (train vs test) reference baseline, and a per-sample out-of-support/novelty score.

papers.title: Beyond Single-Channel: Multichannel Signal Imaging for PPG-to-ECG Reconstruction with Vision Transformers
papers.model_family: Other (ViT encoder-decoder on four-channel PPG signal images; deterministic regression)
papers.datasets: BIDMC PPG and Respiration; CapnoBase
papers.loss_functions: MSE reconstruction loss on ECG image + QRS-complex-enhanced loss (Gaussian weighting around R-peaks, params sigma, beta); total = sum
papers.eval_metrics: PRD; RMSE; HRV of RR, PP, TT intervals (R-HRV, P-HRV, T-HRV, mean/STD differences); QRS area relative error; PR interval relative error; RT interval relative error; RT amplitude-difference relative error
papers.notes: Introduces clinically-oriented paired metrics (QRS area, PR interval, RT interval, RT amplitude errors). Only 30 low-noise records chosen because peak detection is unreliable on noisy P waves (selection bias). BIDMC PRD 42.65 vs CLEP-GAN 71.43. R/P/T-HRV values identical in table (suspicious).
papers.takeaway: Clinical interval/amplitude relative-error metrics (PR, QRS area, RT) map well onto the features module for paired evaluation.

papers.title: Boosting EEG and ECG Classification with Synthetic Biophysical Data Generated via Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP; also vanilla GAN baseline)
papers.datasets: ECG: Kaggle ECG dataset (140-point beats, normal/abnormal labels); EEG: Bird et al. Muse dataset (TP9, AF7, AF8, TP10)
papers.loss_functions: WGAN-GP: critic loss D(fake)-D(real)+lambda*GP (lambda=10); generator -D(fake); post-hoc smoothing (window 10) of synthetic ECG
papers.eval_metrics: classification accuracy (SVM, RF) trained on real tested on real/synthetic/combined, and with real+synthetic training at varying synthetic proportions; PSD plots (EEG); visual inspection
papers.notes: ECG RF accuracy 97% real -> 98.40% with synthetic. Train-on-real/test-on-synthetic (TRTS) used as quality check. Post-hoc smoothing applied to remove GAN spikes, which may mask generator artefacts. No distributional metrics.
papers.takeaway: TRTS (classifier trained on real, tested on synthetic) is a cheap complementary utility metric; flag post-processing that hides artefacts.

papers.title: Classification feasibility test on multi-lead electrocardiography signals generated from single-lead electrocardiography signals
papers.model_family: GAN (pix2pix conditional GAN, U-Net generator, 1-D; 11 per-lead models)
papers.datasets: Asan Medical Center MUSE database (training, ~4M records); PTB-XL (external, classification)
papers.loss_functions: cGAN adversarial loss + L1 reconstruction loss (pix2pix objective G* = argmin max L_cGAN + L_L1)
papers.eval_metrics: Downstream ResNet classification precision; recall; F1-score; accuracy; ROC/AUC (6 classes: normal, AF, LBBB, RBBB, LVH, RVH) comparing generated 12-lead vs real 12-lead vs real lead I; Einthoven-derived lead ablations
papers.notes: Generation fidelity (FD, MSE) evaluated in prior work; here utility only. Surprising: generated 12-lead F1 0.81 > real 12-lead 0.70 on PTB-XL; authors suggest FD/MSE plus Turing test needed. Mixed-in Einthoven-formula leads gave no significant difference.
papers.takeaway: Utility comparison vs. the single-lead input baseline is a useful 'information gain' check for lead-reconstruction models.

papers.title: Classification of ECG Signals Using GAN, SMOTE, and VAE Data Augmentation Methods: Synthetic vs. Real
papers.venue: Bitlis Eren Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Dergisi
papers.model_family: GAN (vanilla GAN, 2D conv) and VAE (2-layer CNN encoder/decoder) compared with SMOTE
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII lead, 4 AAMI classes F/N/S/V, 42 records)
papers.loss_functions: standard minimax GAN loss (Goodfellow); VAE (reparameterization; loss not explicitly stated)
papers.eval_metrics: accuracy; specificity; recall; F1-score of a 2D-CNN classifier under real-only, synthetic-only, train-synthetic-test-real, and real+synthetic settings
papers.notes: Heartbeats processed as 2D images. Real-only 96.5%; synthetic-only (VAE) 100% (train and test on synthetic, trivially optimistic); TSTR best 86.4% with SMOTE; real+synthetic best 98.6% (VAE). No direct fidelity metrics. Patient-dependent (beat-level) split risks leakage.
papers.takeaway: Shows why TSTR must be separated from train/test-on-synthetic; enforce patient-level splits in utility evaluation.

papers.title: Classification of imbalanced ECGs through segmentation models and augmented by conditional diffusion model
papers.model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM, U-Net, classifier-free guidance; 1-D reshaped to 2-D) compared with VAE and SMOTE-Tomek
papers.task: augmentation (class-cond beats for imbalanced arrhythmia classification)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI N/S/V/F, records 102/104/107/217 excluded)
papers.signal_length_s: single heartbeat segments (length not stated in seconds)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM L_simple noise-prediction MSE; VAE baseline: reconstruction + KL (ELBO)
papers.eval_metrics: Cosine similarity between true and predicted noise on test set (diffusion) / between reconstructed and original (VAE); visual morphology inspection; downstream CNN/transformer classifier Precision, Sensitivity, F1, Accuracy, confusion matrix
papers.notes: Weak generative evaluation: cosine similarity of predicted vs true noise is a training-loss proxy, not a sample-quality metric. Augmentation gave +1.23% F1 for minority classes. Mentions prior VAE work using MMD (3.83e-3).
papers.takeaway: Illustrates pitfall of using denoising-loss proxies as quality metrics; ECGEN-Eval should promote sample-level distribution metrics instead.

papers.title: CLEP-GAN: An Innovative Approach to Subject-Independent ECG Reconstruction from PPG Signals
papers.model_family: GAN (CLEP-GAN: Attention U-Net generators + contrastive learning + dual time/frequency discriminators; CLEP-VQGAN variant with VQ-VAE)
papers.datasets: BIDMC PPG and Respiration; CapnoBase TBME RR (resampled 300->125 Hz); ODE-based synthetic ECG-PPG dataset (RSR, SA, AFib)
papers.loss_functions: NT-Xent contrastive loss (PPG->ECG) + reconstruction losses Lp2p, Le2e, Lp2e + VQ dictionary & commitment losses (VQGAN variant) + adversarial losses from time-domain and STFT-spectrogram frequency-domain discriminators; Ltotal = 30·Lgen + 3·Lt + 1·Lf
papers.eval_metrics: RR-interval distribution: relative Histogram Intersection (rHI), relative RMSE, relative EMD, KL divergence, two-sample KS test; waveform RMSE; MAE of heart rate (MAE_HR); HRV (mean RR, SDNN of RR) GT vs reconstruction; Fréchet Distance in feature space; MFLOPs, MParams, inference time
papers.embedding_extractor: not specified (FD 'in feature space', following CardioGAN-type refs)
papers.notes: RR-interval histogram metrics with fixed bin width used to validate the synthetic ODE dataset. Analyses effects of sex/age on reconstruction; warns against indiscriminate dataset augmentation. T-wave reconstruction remains inconsistent. Baselines: CardioGAN, QRS-ED, RDDM.
papers.takeaway: RR-interval distribution comparison with several divergences (HI, EMD, KL, KS) is a simple rhythm-fidelity metric family worth adding.

papers.title: Compact Latent Manifold Translation: A Parameter-Efficient Foundation Model for Cross-Modal and Cross-Frequency Physiological Signal Synthesis
papers.model_family: Other (RVQ-VAE universal tokenizer + Transformer latent translator + latent masked-autoencoder; discrete-codebook foundation model)
papers.datasets: not reported (heterogeneous ECG/PPG datasets; names not found in text)
papers.loss_functions: Stage 1: shape-aware reconstruction L1 + alpha*(1 - cosine similarity) + beta*L1 on temporal gradient (alpha=beta=0.5) + lambda_vq * VQ commitment loss; Stage 2: MSE latent distillation (translator and SR MAE)
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; R-peak detection F1-score; Frechet Distance (FD); Pearson correlation; PSD-RMSE; UMAP latent visualization
papers.notes: R-peak F1 used as a clinical landmark-preservation metric: 0.83 vs 0.37 baseline P2E; FD halved 37.49->16.18. SR: Pearson 0.9956, PSD-RMSE 0.0013, FD 0.0406. Argues MSE regression oversmooths QRS. 0.09B params (efficiency claim).
papers.takeaway: R-peak detection F1 between real and generated signals is a simple landmark-fidelity metric; PSD-RMSE complements PSD JS divergence.

papers.title: Complementarity-Preserving Generative Theory for Multimodal ECG Synthesis: A Quantum-Inspired Approach
papers.model_family: GAN (quantum-inspired Q-CFD-GAN, complex-valued latent, Hermitian interference operator, tri-domain decoder)
papers.task: unconditional (multimodal: time, STFT spectrum, time-frequency scalogram of beats)
papers.datasets: multimodal ECG dataset from Mendeley Data (patient-level 70/15/15 split)
papers.loss_functions: adversarial with gradient penalty + lambda1*CFD complementarity loss (tri-domain complementarity alignment + orthogonality penalty) + lambda2*interference-preserving loss + lambda3*physiological morphology loss (QRS and ST L2 terms)
papers.eval_metrics: embedding variance and excess-variance ratio (pretrained multimodal encoder); classifier-based plausibility gap (KL divergence of pretrained classifier outputs real vs synthetic); tri-domain complementarity retention; RMS energy deviation (%); morphology contraction coefficient; peak-to-peak amplitude, RMS energy and spectral entropy distributions; RMS-P2P joint manifold
papers.embedding_extractor: pretrained multimodal ECG encoder and pretrained ECG classifier (unspecified)
papers.notes: Novel classifier-output KL 'plausibility gap' (0.157 vs 0.214 for MI-GAN) and cross-domain complementarity retention (0.91). Metrics derived from their own theory; single dataset; no TSTR or expert evaluation.
papers.takeaway: Classifier-output KL plausibility gap and P2P/RMS/spectral-entropy distribution plots are easy additions.

papers.title: Condition-fusion-and-hiding denoising diffusion model for electrocardiogram lead reconstruction
papers.model_family: Diffusion (CFH-DDPM: condition-fusion-and-hiding DDPM); baselines VAE, EKGAN, DDPM
papers.datasets: PTB-XL; CPSC2018
papers.n_leads: 12 (input lead I implied by near-perfect lead I scores)
papers.loss_functions: not reported
papers.eval_metrics: Per-lead Sum of Squared Difference (SSD); Percentage Root-mean-square Difference (PRD %); Cosine Similarity (%); Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR dB)
papers.notes: Only supplementary tables available. CFH-DDPM mean PTB-XL: SSD 31.84, PRD 73.78%, COS 68.59%, SNR 4.79 dB; EKGAN has lower PRD (69.78%). Limb leads III/aVF show PRD >100% for all models, showing PRD saturates for poorly predictable leads.
papers.takeaway: Report reconstruction metrics per lead: averages hide that some leads (III, aVF) are essentially unpredictable (PRD>100%).

papers.title: Conditional Electrocardiogram Generation Using Hierarchical Variational Autoencoders
papers.model_family: VAE (hierarchical conditional Nouveau VAE, cNVAE-ECG; also 2D-cNVAE-ECG variant)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (training, binary MI vs SR and multi-label); Georgia and Ningbo (PhysioNet/CinC 2021) for transfer-learning downstream evaluation
papers.loss_functions: NVAE ELBO: hierarchical KL terms + reconstruction likelihood modelled as mixture of discretized logistic distributions
papers.eval_metrics: downstream AUROC of XResNet1d101 classifier: binary (MI vs SR) and multi-label (LAD, LVH, AF, STach, IAVB, SB, TAb) with varying synthetic proportions; transfer learning (pretrain on synthetic/real, fine-tune on Georgia/Ningbo)
papers.notes: Baselines: conditional WaveGAN* and Pulse2Pulse. AUROC gains up to ~2% (1.5% binary, 1.8% with MI addition). Evaluation is utility-only (augmentation ratios 0.1-2.0, pretraining); no distributional or morphology fidelity metrics. Percentile (2.5-97.5) amplitude filtering per lead.
papers.takeaway: Augmentation-ratio sweeps and transfer-learning pretraining are useful utility protocols; complement with fidelity metrics.

papers.title: Data imbalance in cardiac health diagnostics using CECG-GAN
authors: Yang Y, Lan T, Wang Y, Li F, Liu L, Huang X, Gao F, Jiang S, Zhang Z, Chen X.
papers.model_family: GAN (conditional, TimeGAN-style with Transformer encoder/decoder/generator/discriminator; 'CECG-GAN')
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia; CPSC2020
papers.loss_functions: Adversarial (conditional GAN) loss + TimeGAN-style embedding/recovery reconstruction and supervised latent-matching loss (details not formally given)
papers.eval_metrics: PRD; Fréchet Distance (discrete, per-pair); RMSE; MAE; downstream classifier Precision, Recall, F1, Accuracy; per-patient evaluation; comparison to BiLSTM-CNN GAN, LSTM-AE GAN, LSTM-VAE GAN, SimGAN
papers.notes: Abstract reports PRD 55.048 (high, yet claimed 'high similarity'), FD 1.139, RMSE 0.232, MAE 0.166; best patient PRD 21.1. Synthetic samples filtered by whether they improve classifier F1 - risk of selection bias/leakage. FD is pairwise discrete Fréchet, not FID-style.
papers.takeaway: Clarify FD naming (discrete Fréchet vs Fréchet-Gaussian) and warn against classifier-guided sample selection in utility evaluation.

papers.title: Deep conditional generative model for personalization of 12-lead electrocardiograms and cardiovascular risk prediction
authors: Sang Y, Banerjee A, Beetz M, Grau V.
papers.model_family: VAE (conditional VAE, 1D conv encoder/decoder) + Cox proportional-hazards head
papers.task: other (personalised generation conditioned on demographics, heart pose, electrode positions; CVD risk prediction)
papers.datasets: UK Biobank (37,508 volunteers; 21,083 with ECG+MRI; 1,834 with electrode positions); in silico simulations (Mincholé et al.)
papers.signal_length_s: median beat (~600 samples, model input 12x400); 10 s raw available
papers.loss_functions: cVAE ELBO: MSE reconstruction + KL divergence; plus Cox partial-likelihood survival loss; Ltotal = Lrecons + LKL + Lsurv (equal weights)
papers.eval_metrics: qualitative comparison of morphology trends (R/S/T amplitudes per lead) against in silico simulation under heart rotation/translation; C-index for CVD risk; Kaplan-Meier stratification
papers.notes: No quantitative generative-quality metric; validation is lead-wise agreement of amplitude trends with biophysical simulation (often only partially agrees). C-index 0.63-0.65 from latent embeddings.
papers.takeaway: Simulation-consistency (controllability: does changing a condition shift morphology as physics predicts) is a distinct evaluation axis.

papers.title: DiffECG: A Versatile Probabilistic Diffusion Model for ECG Signals Synthesis
papers.venue: IEEE/ACIS International Conference on Software Engineering Research, Management and Applications (SERA)
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM on spectrograms, conditional U-Net; DiffECG)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII lead; classes N, V, F)
papers.signal_length_s: 0.75 (270 samples: 350 ms before / 400 ms after R-peak)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction (epsilon) loss + MSE regression loss between generated and ground-truth signal (imputation/forecasting)
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; FID; DTW; Earth Mover's Distance (EMD); MMD; downstream arrhythmia classifier Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 (train real + synthetic); visual inspection
papers.notes: Per-class (N, V, F) metric tables; FID values ~1e-3 indicate non-standard FID computation (not Inception-based on images). 70/30 signal-wise split. Augmentation compared against 4 GAN baselines with 3 classifiers. Qualitative check only by authors.
papers.takeaway: EMD and per-class reporting are cheap additions; FID without a specified extractor is not comparable across papers.

papers.title: DiffECG: Diffusion Model-Powered Label-Efficient and Personalized Arrhythmia Diagnosis
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM denoising U-Net used as self-supervised feature extractor; NAS-pruned encoder+bottleneck; multimodal feature fusion)
papers.task: other (diffusion-based self-supervised representation learning for arrhythmia detection; not a synthesis paper)
papers.datasets: CPSC 2018; Chapman; PTB; Georgia; LTAF (long-term AF)
papers.loss_functions: standard DDPM noise-prediction loss for pre-training; classifier fine-tuning (cross-entropy); zeroth-order optimisation of noise step t using proposed gamma (loss-sensitivity) metric
papers.eval_metrics: macro F1; macro accuracy (generalization cross-dataset and per-subject personalization)
papers.notes: No synthetic-ECG quality evaluation at all; diffusion denoiser used only as a feature extractor. Relevant mainly as evidence that diffusion U-Net features are discriminative (possible embedding backbone).
papers.takeaway: Diffusion denoiser features could serve as an alternative embedding for FED-style metrics; otherwise little eval relevance.

papers.title: DiffuSETS: 12-lead ECG Generation Conditioned on Clinical Text Reports and Patient-Specific Information
papers.model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM U-Net with cross-attention on LLM text embeddings + patient info; VAE latent space)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (+ MIMIC-IV-Clinical for age/sex); PTB-XL (external)
papers.loss_functions: Latent DDPM noise-prediction MSE ||ε-ε̂(z_t,t,c)||²; VAE: MSE reconstruction + λ·KL divergence
papers.eval_metrics: Signal level: FID; improved precision/recall/F1 (Kynkäänniemi manifold) on embeddings; Feature level: heart-rate MAE (conditioned vs generated HR); Diagnostic level: CLIP score (text-ECG alignment); clinical Turing test (2 cardiologists, 50 real+50 generated); expert semantic-alignment check (100 ECGs, 76%); heart-age correlation via AnyECG (r=0.594); downstream augmentation classification for rare classes
papers.embedding_extractor: pretrained Net1D ECG encoder (FID, P/R); Net1D + text encoder CLIP-style model for CLIP score
papers.notes: Proposes three-level benchmark (signal/feature/diagnostic). Argues MAE unreliable due to phase shifts, uses manifold P/R instead. MIMIC: FID 23.6, F1 0.894, HR-MAE 4.15, CLIP 0.812. Baselines WaveGAN, Pulse2Pulse, SSSD-ECG on PTB-XL.
papers.takeaway: Adopt three-level protocol: embedding FID + manifold precision/recall, condition-adherence MAE (e.g., HR), and text/label alignment via a CLIP-style ECG-text encoder.

papers.title: DiSR-ECG: Residual Shifting Conditional Diffusion for Robust ECG Super-Resolution
papers.model_family: Diffusion (residual-shifting conditional diffusion, ResShift-style, Mamba temporal backbone; DiSR-ECG)
papers.task: super-resolution (50 Hz -> 500 Hz, with noise robustness)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (train/in-domain); Chapman-Shaoxing (zero-shot cross-dataset); MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test DB (noise injection)
papers.loss_functions: L1 reconstruction + scale-invariant SDR (negative SI-SDR, lambda_SI=0.02)
papers.eval_metrics: MSE; Cosine Similarity (CoS); SNR (dB); Maximum Absolute Deviation (MAD); paired-sample t-test significance
papers.notes: 15 diffusion steps; 10-sample ensemble at inference. Baselines: linear interpolation, SRECG, DCAE-SR, MSECG. Significance testing (p<0.05) of improvements is a good practice. Ablation: removing SI-SDR lowers SNR. Cross-dataset generalization emphasised.
papers.takeaway: Add SI-SDR / cosine similarity / max-abs-deviation for paired tasks, plus paired significance tests.

papers.title: ECG Generation Based on Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, Attention U-Net; signal-, STFT-spectrogram- (Griffin-Lim) and wavelet-subband variants)
papers.task: class-cond / augmentation (beats N, LBBB, RBBB, PVC)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII; records 102/104/107/217 excluded)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction L2 (epsilon MSE)
papers.eval_metrics: DTW; Euclidean distance (ED); Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC); KL divergence (KLD) - all between average synthetic beat and average real beat; visual inspection
papers.notes: Metrics computed on class-mean templates only, so diversity/mode collapse is invisible. Best: ED 4.37, DTW 17.09 (direct signal diffusion); PCC 0.972, KLD 0.0094 (wavelet diffusion).
papers.takeaway: Template (mean-beat) PCC/DTW is a useful cheap fidelity check but must be paired with diversity metrics.

papers.title: ECG Synthesis via Diffusion-Based State Space Augmented Transformer
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM with State Space Augmented Transformer denoiser, DSAT-ECG; SSSD-ECG-like)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (patient-wise split 17,441/2,193/2,203)
papers.n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 derived via Einthoven/Goldberger)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM simplified noise-prediction MSE
papers.eval_metrics: average DTW; average MMD (Gaussian kernel); 'authenticity': multilabel accuracy and macro AUROC of a ResNet-1D classifier trained on real data evaluated on synthetic vs real test sets (TRTS)
papers.notes: DTW 7.174, MMD 4.603e-3 vs SSSD-ECG 7.481/4.784e-3; TRTS acc 95.84/AUROC 94.56 vs real 96.38/94.67. Pitfall: metrics computed in batches of 16 samples — tiny-sample MMD/DTW are noisy. Admits synthetic data cannot fully replace real for training.
papers.takeaway: TRTS (real-trained classifier scored on synthetic vs real) is a cheap class-conditional check; warn about small-batch MMD estimates.

papers.title: ECG-WM: A Physiology-Informed ECG World Model for Clinical Intervention Simulation
papers.model_family: Hybrid (latent DDPM world model over frozen pretrained ECG VAE, with cardiac-ODE physiological energy regularization; VLM proposes interventions)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG + MIMIC-IV-Clinical (17,493 patients, 108,980 patient-drug episodes); drug-response ECG datasets (ECGRDVQ and related FDA studies; 43 subjects, 8 regimens); in-house MIMIC-IV verapamil OOD set
papers.loss_functions: VAE: reconstruction + KL (pretrained, frozen); diffusion: epsilon-prediction MSE + lambda_EPK (0.1) * latent energy ||z0_hat - Pi(e_EPK)||^2 to ODE-derived physiological anchor
papers.eval_metrics: latent and signal MSE/MAE/RMSE (single and multi-step rollouts, rollout-oracle error); interval-normality Accuracy/Recall for QTc (Bazett), PR, Tpeak-Tend; OOD latent/signal error; Delta-risk Pearson, Spearman, sign agreement of ECG-FM diagnostic-score change; sample dispersion under prior perturbation
papers.embedding_extractor: frozen ECG-FM foundation model (McKeen et al. 2025) producing 17 label probabilities as risk proxy
papers.notes: States MSE insufficient; uses clinical interval-category agreement (QTc<=450/470 ms, PR 120-200 ms, Tpeak-Tend 80-113 ms; correct only if all labels match). Diagnostic-change agreement via frozen foundation model: Pearson 0.620 vs DADM 0.266. Compares WGAN, StyleGAN, ODE-GAN, TTS-CGAN, CECG-GAN, Diffusets, SE-Diff, DADM.
papers.takeaway: Clinical interval normal-range agreement and foundation-model label-probability agreement are strong conditional-fidelity metrics.

papers.title: ECGrecover: a Deep Learning Approach for Electrocardiogram Signal Completion
papers.model_family: Other (U-Net regression; compared with GAN baselines EKGAN, Pix2Pix, and CopyPaste)
papers.task: lead-reconstruction + imputation (missing segments within a lead; full leads from a single lead)
papers.datasets: Generepol (15,119 ECGs, 989 healthy subjects, before/after Sotalol); PTB-XL; LUDB
papers.loss_functions: Composite L = MSE + alpha * Pearson-correlation loss (1 - r); alpha ablated in {0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, inf}
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; maximum absolute error (MAE); DTW; Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC); delta-QT distance (neurokit2 Q and T peak detection per beat); SQI Avg-QRS and SQI Fuzzy (% unacceptable); downstream TdP-risk DenseNet accuracy with augmentation (5 seeds); statistical tests (p<2e-16)
papers.notes: Delta-QT shows CopyPaste trivially preserves QT, a metric pitfall. Hybrid MSE+Pearson loss balances amplitude and synchrony; Pearson-only gives high PCC but poor other metrics. Expert cardiologists curated data. Augmentation raised TdP accuracy 92.47 -> 93.84%.
papers.takeaway: Adopt delta-QT (and other interval deltas) via neurokit2 plus SQI scores (Avg-QRS, Fuzzy) as clinical fidelity checks.

papers.title: ECGTwin: Personalized ECG Generation Using Controllable Diffusion Model
papers.model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM, DiT or U-Net backbone, AdaX condition injector; contrastive Individual Base Extractor)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (+ MIMIC-IV-Clinical); PTB-XL (external)
papers.loss_functions: Stage 1: symmetric CLIP-style InfoNCE contrastive loss (cosine similarity, learnable τ) on same-patient ECG pairs; Stage 2: DDPM noise-prediction MSE; pre-trained VAE decoder
papers.eval_metrics: FID; improved precision/recall/F1 (Kynkäänniemi); HR-MAE; CLIP score; intra-/inter-individual similarity score (cosine); silhouette coefficient; t-SNE; downstream personalized normal/abnormal classification accuracy and macro-F1 (patient-wise and population-wise)
papers.embedding_extractor: same as DiffuSETS three-level protocol (pretrained ECG encoder; not restated)
papers.notes: Reuses DiffuSETS three-level evaluation; adds identity-preservation metrics (similarity score = mean intra-patient minus inter-patient cosine; silhouette). Baselines LAVQ, DiffuSETS-p. CLIP lower on PTB-XL due to German reports.
papers.takeaway: For conditional/personalized generation, add identity-preservation metrics (intra- vs inter-subject embedding similarity, silhouette).

papers.title: End-to-end non-invasive ECG signal generation from PPG signal: a self-supervised learning approach
papers.model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP with Transformer-based generator/discriminator; self-supervised pretraining of discriminator via signal-transformation recognition)
papers.datasets: Who is Alyx? (VR dataset, ECG 130 Hz / Empatica PPG 64 Hz); MIMIC III matched waveform (125 Hz); MIMIC PERform AF (AF detection); pretraining: BIDMC, CapnoBase, WESAD
papers.signal_length_s: windows of 4-160 s (best 64 s Who is Alyx?, 96 s MIMIC III); 30 s for AF task
papers.loss_functions: WGAN-GP adversarial (Wasserstein + gradient penalty, lambda tuned); self-supervised pretext loss: six-way signal-transformation recognition (noise, scaling, temporal inversion, permutation, negation, time-warping)
papers.eval_metrics: Frechet Distance (discrete curve FD); RMSE (mV); Pearson correlation; MAE of heart rate (MAEHR, generated ECG vs PPG); MMD^2 and squared Energy Distance with permutation-test p-values on embeddings; t-SNE; AF detection accuracy/precision/recall/F1 with varying synthetic proportions
papers.embedding_extractor: own Transformer discriminator (512-d penultimate layer)
papers.notes: LOSO evaluation. Best RMSE 0.168 mV, rho 0.952 (MIMIC III, 96 s). HR error reduced 83.9%/72.4% vs PPG. 'FD' here is discrete Frechet curve distance, not FID-style. MMD^2 0.011 (p=0.84). Pitfall: using own discriminator as embedding extractor for MMD/ED is biased.
papers.takeaway: Adopt permutation-test p-values for MMD/energy distance and HR-error (MAEHR); disambiguate curve-FD vs Gaussian FD in naming.

papers.title: Evaluating the feasibility of 12-lead electrocardiogram reconstruction from limited leads using deep learning
papers.model_family: GAN (Pulse2Pulse/pix2pix-inspired U-Net generator, WGAN-GP) and U-Net (MSE) baseline
papers.datasets: PTB-XL v1.0.3 (9514 individuals; test 952 normal ECGs)
papers.loss_functions: GAN: WGAN-GP adversarial (with gradient clipping) + L1 reconstruction; U-Net: MSE
papers.eval_metrics: Per-lead RMSE; GE MUSE 12SL measurements (RR, QT, PR, QRS duration, R/S/T peak, ST amplitudes); Student t-test (means); F-test (variances); Bland-Altman plots; R2/Pearson between error and true amplitude (regression-to-mean); inter-lead marker correlations real vs reconstructed
papers.notes: Key metric criticism: low RMSE hides regression-to-the-mean. Reconstructed amplitudes have reduced variance (F-test p<0.05); error vs true amplitude R2=0.92 (V3); inter-lead R-amplitude R2 I-V3 0.04 real vs 0.49 reconstructed. Concludes not clinically usable.
papers.takeaway: Add variance-ratio (F-test), error-vs-amplitude correlation and inter-lead correlation preservation checks to detect regression-to-mean.

papers.title: Evaluating the Quality of CycleGAN Generated ECG Data for Myocardial Infarction Classification
papers.model_family: GAN (CycleGAN style transfer, 2 CycleGANs / 4 generators)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (10,776 ECGs: NORM, ASMI, IMI)
papers.loss_functions: CycleGAN losses (adversarial + cycle consistency, as in Zhu et al.; not detailed)
papers.eval_metrics: 95% confidence-band plots per lead; UMAP 2D density/scatter (fit on real); GAN-train score; GAN-test score (vs baselines); ST-segment amplitude comparison via modified Hotelling T² simultaneous 95% intervals per lead
papers.notes: Negative result: GAN-train 62% vs baseline 98%; GAN-test 81% vs baseline 89%; ST amplitudes significantly different in all conditions; distributions overlapped only in tails. Warns image-domain GANs cannot simply be adapted to ECG.
papers.takeaway: Add GAN-train/GAN-test with baselines and per-lead ST-amplitude Hotelling-style intervals; confidence-band plots are a cheap visual diagnostic.

papers.title: f-GAN: A frequency-domain-constrained generative adversarial network for PPG to ECG synthesis
papers.model_family: GAN (f-GAN: U-Net-style encoder-decoder generator, standard adversarial loss + frequency-domain constraint)
papers.datasets: PPG-DaLiA (15 participants, subject-disjoint 9/3/3 split)
papers.loss_functions: Original GAN minimax adversarial loss + lambda_freq (0.1) * L1 distance between FFT amplitude spectra (excluding DC) of generated and real ECG
papers.eval_metrics: Heart-rate MAPE (peak detector on synthetic vs real ECG); number of heart-rate estimation failure cases (peak detector fails); comparison with PPG peak-detection HR baseline; qualitative waveform inspection
papers.notes: Argues HR error is more interpretable than RMSE. Novel 'pipeline-compatibility' metric: count of segments where standard peak detection fails on synthetic ECG. 31 random seeds with t-tests (p=0.005). Frequency constraint lowers HR error ~2% and variance.
papers.takeaway: Add peak-detection failure rate on synthetic ECGs and multi-seed statistical testing to ECGEN-Eval.

papers.title: FlowECG: Using Flow Matching to Create a More Efficient ECG Signal Generator
papers.model_family: FlowMatching (rectified/linear-path flow matching on SSSD-ECG S4 backbone)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL
papers.n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 derived)
papers.loss_functions: Flow matching L2 velocity regression ||f(x_t,c,t)-(x1-x0)||^2 (baseline SSSD-ECG: diffusion MSE noise prediction)
papers.eval_metrics: DTW; 1-Wasserstein distance on handcrafted statistical/temporal/spectral features; MMD; spectral similarity score 1/(1+mean W(PSD_real,PSD_gen)); NFE vs quality curves; all per-lead averaged
papers.embedding_extractor: handcrafted features (statistical moments, temporal, spectral)
papers.notes: At 200 NFE: MMD 21.09 vs 80.70 (SSSD-ECG), DTW 83.96 vs 73.49, W 0.62 vs 1.03, SimScore 0.37 vs 0.30. Comparable quality at 10-25 NFE. Explicitly notes field lacks standardized protocols. No utility or clinical metrics.
papers.takeaway: Quality-vs-NFE (sampling budget) curves and PSD-Wasserstein spectral similarity are worth adding; ECGEN-Eval already has DTW/MMD/PSD.

papers.title: Generating Precordial-lead Electrocardiogram from Smartwatch
papers.model_family: GAN (pix2pix-style U-Net generator, 5-layer conv discriminator; one model per precordial lead)
papers.datasets: Asan Medical Center 12-lead records (training); 10 healthy volunteers, Galaxy Watch4 + standard 12-lead (100 test recordings)
papers.loss_functions: not reported
papers.eval_metrics: Fréchet distance (FD, per lead); MSE (per lead)
papers.notes: Mean FD 15.46, MSE 0.0937; V1 best (FD 4.69), V3/V4 worst (~21). FD formula given as Gaussian Fréchet (mean+covariance), described as curve similarity — ambiguous. Very small real-world test set.
papers.takeaway: Report per-lead FD; be explicit whether 'FD' is curve Fréchet or Gaussian Fréchet — literature conflates them.

papers.title: Generating Realistic Multi-Beat ECG Signals
papers.model_family: Hybrid (beat-level time-series Diffusion with prompt bases + multivariate feature-sequence generator + feature-guided beat matching/stitching)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Supraventricular Arrhythmia Database (main); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (additional test)
papers.signal_length_s: single beats ~100-200 samples; long-form sequences (e.g., 100 beats)
papers.loss_functions: not reported
papers.eval_metrics: Beat level: DTW, Frechet distance, Euclidean distance, RMSE, MAE, MSE, PRD between average beats; average KL, JS divergence, MMD, Wasserstein, KS statistic, mean/variance/skewness differences. Features: per-feature KL, MMD, Wasserstein, KS, mean difference; feature correlation matrices; density-difference heatmap. Utility: TSTR accuracy/precision/recall/F1 (SVM, Balanced SVM, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, and others); R-amplitude matching rate
papers.notes: Long-form ECGs outperform end-to-end long diffusion in TSTR. Pitfall: many fidelity metrics computed only between AVERAGE beats (e.g., DTW 2.07, PRD 8.53), which hides diversity/mode collapse. Inter-feature correlation preservation (RR, P/Q/T intervals) is a useful multi-beat check.
papers.takeaway: Compare inter-beat feature distributions (KS/Wasserstein per interval) and feature-correlation matrices; avoid average-beat-only metrics.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Modeling Bio-Electric Fields in Medicine: A Review of EEG, ECG, EMG, and EOG Applications
papers.model_family: Survey (GANs for EEG/ECG/EMG/EOG)
papers.datasets: catalogued: MIT-BIH, PTB-XL and others across modalities
papers.loss_functions: Catalogues GAN loss variants with formulas: WGAN (Wasserstein), WGAN-GP (gradient penalty), BGAN, EBGAN, LSGAN, conditional GAN/CWGAN; mentions physiological constraints in GAN losses and feature-loss functions for denoising
papers.eval_metrics: Catalogued (synthesis): PRD; RMSE; FD; MAE; DTW; Fréchet/Euclidean distance; SSIM; FID; IS; sliced Wasserstein distance; MMD; Kappa; classification accuracy/F1/AUC; (denoising): SNR; RRMSE (time/frequency); CC; PSNR; MI; PRD
papers.notes: Proposes task-specific evaluation framework; flags pitfalls: subject-wise data leakage inflating classifier-based quality proxies and 'metric-task mismatch' (fidelity judged only by statistical similarity rather than preservation of diagnostic features). Calls for standardized protocols and physiological constraints in losses.
papers.takeaway: Encode the subject-wise split warning and diagnostic-feature preservation (clinical features) alongside statistical similarity metrics.

papers.title: Graph-Based ECG Synthesis with Activation-Consistency Certification and Diagnostics-Aware Morphology Curation
papers.model_family: Other (biophysical graph-based simulator: Eikonal-template ET and pseudo-diffusion reaction-Eikonal RE backends; not a deep generative model)
papers.task: other (mechanistic synthetic ECG generation + curation; synthetic pretraining)
papers.datasets: simulated 12-lead ECGs; PTB-XL+ (delineation fine-tuning/evaluation)
papers.signal_length_s: single beats; 12 s concatenated traces for pretraining
papers.loss_functions: none for generator (simulation); delineation segmentation model loss not reported
papers.eval_metrics: Bellman residual certificate (activation-time consistency); R² of RE vs Eikonal activation times; activation-order diagnostics; P/QRS/T amplitudes, intervals, polarity checks, morphology-failure flags; recovery plausibility score; feature-space coverage (fraction of occupied feature bins); acceptance yield; P/QRS/T delineation IoU after synthetic pretraining on 1-10% PTB-XL+ labels
papers.notes: Two-stage diagnostics (metric computation separated from acceptance policy). Acceptance 658/2000 RE vs 578/2000 ET; coverage 0.09888 vs 0.09248. Synthetic pretraining stabilised low-label delineation (T-wave IoU std ≤0.003 vs 0.247). Not a learned generator; relevant mostly for curation/validity filters.
papers.takeaway: Hard validity filters (flatline, missing QRS, inverted QRS) + binned feature-space coverage are useful sanity/diversity metrics.

papers.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic ECG Generation via Mel-Spectrogram Informed Diffusion Training
papers.model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG backbone, score-based diffusion with structured state-space layers; MIDT-ECG)
papers.task: class-cond (diagnosis + demographic conditioning: age, gender, height, weight)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (standard patient-level splits)
papers.loss_functions: MSE denoising loss + beta * L1 multi-resolution Mel-spectrogram loss (multi-window STFT, Mel-warped)
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; MSE; SNR; Fourier distance; Hausdorff distance; SSIM; Membership Inference Risk (MIR); Nearest-Neighbor Adversarial Accuracy (NNAA); inter-lead Pearson correlation matrix error; clinical feature distributions (e.g. QT); label faithfulness (real-trained classifier agreement); downstream AUROC in data substitution/augmentation (synthetic-only, mixed folds); outlier analysis (Q3+3IQR); visual Turing-style comparison
papers.embedding_extractor: classifier trained on real PTB-XL for faithfulness/AUROC (architecture not detailed in extracted text)
papers.notes: Proposes multi-pillar benchmark (fidelity, personalization, privacy, utility). Synthetic-only training AUROC 0.640 vs SSSD-ECG 0.541. Inter-lead correlation-matrix error is a key metric. Faithfulness used as both metric and filter. Gains 4-8% over baseline. Outlier lead-distribution analysis.
papers.takeaway: Adopt inter-lead correlation-matrix error, NNAA/MIR privacy metrics, and classifier-based label faithfulness.

papers.title: Improving Diffusion Models for ECG Imputation with an Augmented Template Prior
papers.model_family: Diffusion (PulseDiff: CSDI and SSSD-S4 backbones conditioned on augmented pulse-template prior)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (PulseImpute splits: 8730 train / 2176 val / 10931 test)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE conditioned on observed values and template prior p
papers.eval_metrics: MSE (imputed vs ground truth); downstream multi-label classification macro-AUC (rhythm, form, diagnostic) with pretrained xResNet1d; beat detection F1, precision, sensitivity (SWT detector, 50 ms tolerance); evaluated at 10-50% missingness (transient and extended)
papers.embedding_extractor: pretrained xResNet1d classifiers from PulseImpute (downstream only)
papers.notes: Follows PulseImpute benchmark. Transient 30%: PulseDiff-SSSDS4 MSE 0.0021; extended: 0.0192, deterministic BDC transformer still best. Notes diffusion trained on noise-space loss underperforms on long gaps.
papers.takeaway: Beat-detection F1 with tolerance window and pretrained-classifier AUC on generated signals are reusable checks.

papers.title: Introducing a Comprehensive Framework for Synthetic ECG Validation
authors: Zanchi B, Monachino G, Metaldi M, Conte G, Meystre S, Faraci FD.
papers.venue: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
papers.model_family: EvalOnly (validation framework; applied to Pulse2Pulse GAN Brugada ECGs)
papers.datasets: Private Brugada type-I 12-lead ECGs (21 patients, 1122 10-s windows with 50% overlap) vs 1122 synthetic
papers.loss_functions: n/a (Pulse2Pulse WGAN-GP referenced)
papers.eval_metrics: Four layers: (1) visual inspection; (2) morphology via NeuroKit on lead II: RR, PR, QRS, QT, QTc (Bazett), P/QRS/T axes, Mann-Whitney U; (3) similarity: Euclidean distance, maximum absolute error, cosine similarity, MSE, RMSE, NRMSE, RMSPE, kernel MMD, KL divergence, DTW (KMMD/KL/DTW on II, V1, V2) benchmarked against R-vs-R intra-subject and inter-subject distances; (4) expert cardiologist scoring
papers.notes: Only supplementary text available. Key idea: synthetic-to-real distance should lie between real intra-subject and inter-subject variability (R-vs-R benchmarking). Careful statistics: patient-level median aggregation to respect independence. Mentions EU AI Act/GMLP as validation gate.
papers.takeaway: Adopt R-vs-R reference bands: express every distance metric relative to real intra-subject and inter-subject baselines.

papers.title: Leveraging Statistical Shape Priors in GAN-Based ECG Synthesis
papers.model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP generating statistical shape model parameters; 2D shape prior of temporal+amplitude variation; DTW-based k-means; LSTM discriminator)
papers.task: class-cond (heartbeat classes N, V, F); augmentation
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII)
papers.signal_length_s: single heartbeat, 270 samples (350 ms pre / 400 ms post R-peak)
papers.loss_functions: WGAN-GP (Wasserstein adversarial + gradient penalty, lambda=10)
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; MSE; Earth Mover's Distance (EMD); DTW (ms); downstream precision/recall/F1 of three heartbeat classifiers in 5 augmentation settings; cardiologist visual Turing test (3 cardiologists, real vs synthetic and class identification)
papers.notes: Includes useful literature table of metrics used by prior ECG GANs (MMD, DTW, FD, PRD, RMSE, PCC, DTW_D, MVDTW). Cardiologists recognized ~90-96.6% of real beats as real and classified synthetic classes correctly. Class F F1 rose to 0.93 with augmentation.
papers.takeaway: Per-class metrics + small cardiologist Turing test; EMD in mV and DTW in ms are interpretable units worth reporting.

papers.title: Lightweight Multi-task CNN for ECG Diagnosis with GRU-Diffusion
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM U-Net with embedded 16-layer GRU, 'GRU-Diffusion') + lightweight multi-task CNN classifier (DFNet)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (12 classes); PTB Diagnostic ECG Database (9 classes, 12 standard leads)
papers.loss_functions: Generator: standard DDPM objective (not explicitly stated); classifier: cross-entropy for two tasks + L2 regularization
papers.eval_metrics: FID (Fréchet distance on PCA-reduced signals); mean and std of DTW on randomly paired real/generated signals; KL divergence between Welch PSDs; downstream Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1; params/FLOPs
papers.embedding_extractor: PCA projection (no pretrained network)
papers.notes: 'FID' computed on PCA features of raw signals, not an Inception/ECG network - naming inconsistency. Reports 99.72% (MIT-BIH) and 99.89% (PTB) accuracy. Uses both mean and std of random-pair DTW as diversity/alignment indicator.
papers.takeaway: PSD-KL via Welch and DTW std (as spread indicator) are cheap complements; label PCA-based FD clearly as such.

papers.title: MedFlow: Class-Aware Multi-Scale Generation for Medical Time-Series Synthesis
papers.model_family: FlowMatching (class-aware multi-scale flow matching over VQ multi-scale token embeddings with Token Marginal Guidance; MedFlow)
papers.task: class-cond (medical time series incl. ECG; imbalanced classes)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III; eICU (EHR); APAVA (EEG); PTB Diagnostic ECG (Medformer split, 108/29/61 subjects)
papers.loss_functions: Stage 1 tokenizer: MSE reconstruction + cosine commitment loss (EMA codebooks); Stage 2: categorical endpoint cross-entropy loss (class-weighted) + structured-source prior regularizer (no direct velocity regression)
papers.eval_metrics: TSTR AUROC; TSTR AUPRC; Discriminative Score (post-hoc GRU); Predictive Score; Context-FID (TS2Vec encoder, dim 320); t-SNE overlap; feature-wise moment, tail-quantile and minority-class statistic discrepancies; sampling throughput
papers.embedding_extractor: TS2Vec encoder fitted on real data (Context-FID); GRU for discriminative/predictive scores
papers.notes: For PTB ECG only TSTR AUROC/AUPRC reported; DS/PS/C-FID reported for EHR tasks. Claims avg -88.6% C-FID and 3.8x throughput vs TarDiff. Emphasises that global fidelity metrics can hide minority-class/tail failures.
papers.takeaway: Add per-class / tail-quantile fidelity and Context-FID (TS2Vec) as a domain-agnostic embedding metric alongside ECG-specific FED.

papers.title: Minority class-aware multiclass arrhythmia detection using conditional GAN augmentation
authors: Tiwari A, Kishore J, Singh R.
papers.model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP with auxiliary classifier in critic; 1D transposed-conv generator)
papers.task: class-cond / augmentation (minority S and F beats)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI 5 classes N, S, V, F, Q)
papers.loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss + gradient penalty + auxiliary classifier (cross-entropy) loss in critic; downstream classifier cross-entropy
papers.eval_metrics: DTW; SSIM (synthetic vs real beats); visual P-QRS-T inspection; downstream hierarchical multi-stream / ResNet34 classifier accuracy, per-class and macro F1, per-class AUC/ROC, 5-fold cross-validation; inference latency, GFLOPs, memory, power on Jetson Nano/Raspberry Pi 5
papers.notes: Augmenting S and F to 10,000 each: macro F1 0.78 -> 0.94, F-class F1 +38%, S +28%. GAN checkpoint chosen by lowest critic loss and best downstream macro F1 on validation (selection on utility). Fidelity metrics (DTW, SSIM) only briefly reported.
papers.takeaway: Utility via per-class minority F1 gains is the main signal; fidelity metrics are thin - typical of augmentation papers.

papers.title: MM-DADM: Multimodal Drug-Aware Diffusion Model for Virtual Clinical Trials
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM backbone with pharmacokinetic ODE fusion via dynamic cross-attention + counterfactual drug-aware ControlNet-style CDC-Net; contrastive causal feature encoder)
papers.task: other-modality2ECG / class-cond (drug- and demographics-conditioned post-dose ECG from pre-dose ECG; virtual clinical trials)
papers.datasets: ECGRDVQ and ECGDMMLD (FDA drug trials; 9,443 12-lead ECGs, 44 subjects, 8 regimens)
papers.n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; 4 limb leads derived)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE (L_bb, L_real) + lambda*causal guidance loss L_cau (1 - cosine sim to drug prototypes, lambda=0.1) for counterfactual samples; supervised contrastive loss L_con for the causal feature encoder
papers.eval_metrics: accuracy/recall of normal-vs-abnormal status agreement on QTc (Bazett), PR, Tpeak-Tend intervals (single and multi-indicator); Fréchet ResNet Distance (FRD); RMSE; cardiologist real-vs-generated discrimination accuracy (10 cardiologists, 100 ECGs per lead per method); downstream ResNet-1D drug-administration classification with 100/200/500 synthetic augmentations
papers.embedding_extractor: 1D ResNet pretrained on PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2017 (final FC layer output) for FRD
papers.notes: FRD 0.2431, RMSE 0.0127 vs SSSD-ECG 0.4719/0.0312 and FlowECG 0.5164. Expert Turing test: ideal is ~50% accuracy; MM-DADM near chance. Clinical-interval threshold agreement (normal/abnormal) is a novel clinically-grounded metric. Compares 10 baselines.
papers.takeaway: Adopt FRD with a pretrained 1D ResNet, interval-category agreement (QTc/PR/Tpeak-Tend normal ranges), and a Turing-test protocol.

papers.title: ODE-Constrained Generative Modeling of Cardiac Dynamics for 12-Lead ECG Synthesis
papers.model_family: GAN (MultiODE-GAN: WaveGAN-based WGAN with ODE (McSharry EDM) physics constraints)
papers.datasets: Georgia 12-Lead ECG Challenge (G12EC); PTB-XL; private LVSD dataset (real-world evaluation)
papers.signal_length_s: single heartbeat (L=300 samples, NeuroKit2 segmentation of 10-s records)
papers.loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss + λ_EUL·Euler Loss = intra-lead Euler loss (ODE residual vs McSharry EDM) + inter-lead Euler loss (Einthoven/derivative consistency), weighting δ=0.6
papers.eval_metrics: Downstream ResNet classifier specificity at fixed sensitivity (real vs real+synthetic, paired t-test); AUROC; AUPRC; inter-lead MSE (Einthoven law consistency); KL divergence and MMD in pretrained ResNet feature space; LVSD detection vs six cardiologists
papers.embedding_extractor: pretrained ResNet-based ECG encoder (KL, MMD)
papers.notes: Inter-lead Einthoven MSE is a physiology-consistency metric. Baselines: SimGAN-extended, SSSD-ECG. KL<0.5 and MMD<0.01 for all abnormalities. Augmentation-only (TRTR vs TR+S) evaluation; no TSTR.
papers.takeaway: Add an Einthoven/Goldberger inter-lead consistency metric (e.g., MSE of I - (II - III)) for 12-lead synthetic data.

papers.title: Optimization of generative-adversarial networks for the synthesis of electrocardiograms by adaptive quantization
papers.venue: Herald of Dagestan State Technical University Technical Sciences
papers.model_family: GAN (MeGAN: BiLSTM generator, CNN discriminator) + post-training weight quantization (AGWR vs Min-Max)
papers.datasets: stated as MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (described as 10 s, 500 Hz, 12-lead, which is inconsistent with MIT-BIH)
papers.loss_functions: standard GAN adversarial (BCE, sigmoid discriminator)
papers.eval_metrics: Frechet Distance (Gaussian on feature space); PSNR; SSIM; Pearson correlation (quantized vs original model outputs); memory consumption
papers.embedding_extractor: not specified ('feature space of the generated layer')
papers.notes: Russian-language paper. FD: MeGAN 0.963 vs RNN-AE GAN 0.969, LSTM-VAE GAN 0.975; quantized 0.964 with ~75% memory reduction at 4-bit. Questionable claim that FD 0.9-1.0 indicates good quality; dataset description inconsistent. PSNR 29.81, SSIM 0.9427 compare quantized vs unquantized outputs.
papers.takeaway: Example of FD values without stated embedding model; ECGEN-Eval should report extractor and scale for every Frechet metric.

papers.title: PDE-Driven Spatiotemporal Generative Modeling for Multilead ECG Synthesis
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.model_family: GAN (PDE-based physics generator, 'PhysioPDE-GAN', reaction-diffusion SA/AV/HP subsystems over lead lattice)
papers.datasets: Georgia 12-Lead ECG Challenge (G12EC); PTB-XL (generalization)
papers.signal_length_s: single heartbeat cycles segmented from 10 s recordings
papers.loss_functions: Non-saturating adversarial loss + coupled PDE residual loss (forward-Euler derivative vs learned response, weighted per SA/AV/HP) + temporal gating loss (Frobenius penalty on activity outside P/PR/QRS-T masks); standard discriminator loss
papers.eval_metrics: Downstream classifier specificity at fixed sensitivity on real held-out test set (ResNet and attention-ResNet), real vs real+synthetic augmentation across baselines (DCGAN, WaveGAN, ME-GAN, MultiODE-GAN, SSSD-ECG); 5-fold cross-validated paired t-test; qualitative beat comparison
papers.notes: Only utility (TRTR vs augmented) evaluated; no direct fidelity/distribution metrics. Patient-wise split enforced. Reporting specificity at fixed sensitivity is a clinically interpretable protocol. NeuroKit2 for beat segmentation.
papers.takeaway: Specificity-at-fixed-sensitivity augmentation protocol with paired t-tests is a good utility-evaluation template.

papers.title: PENGUIN: General Vital Sign Reconstruction from PPG with Flow Matching State Space Model
papers.model_family: FlowMatching (OT-CFM with dual-stream S5 state-space Flow-SSM blocks; Heun sampler, 25 steps)
papers.datasets: PPG-DaLiA; WildPPG (ECG); BIDMC; WESAD (resp); UCI-BP; MIMIC-BP (ABP)
papers.loss_functions: conditional flow matching loss (OT-CFM, L2 velocity regression)
papers.eval_metrics: HR Error (MAE of heart rate in bpm, Hamilton detector, 8 s window); RR Error; SBP/DBP Error; qualitative waveform comparison; ablation
papers.notes: ECG reconstruction judged only by HR MAE (15.64 bpm DaLiA, 12.97 WildPPG) — no waveform-level metrics; cross-subject 6:1:1 split. Baselines: CycleGAN, RDDM, RespDiff, PaPaGei-S.
papers.takeaway: Derived-physiology errors (HR MAE) are an easy clinical paired metric, but alone are insufficient for morphology.

papers.title: Personalized Synthetic Electrocardiograms with Outcomes
papers.model_family: Other (U-Net denoising generator trained with MSE; GAN-derived without discriminator; personalized 1:1 synthesis from noisy original)
papers.task: other (personalized 1:1 synthetic 12-lead ECG with linked patient characteristics and outcomes; privacy-preserving data sharing)
papers.datasets: GESUS and LOFUS cohorts (training); Danish Inter99 cohort (testing, 6,612 ECGs)
papers.loss_functions: Point-wise MSE between denoised output and original noise-free ECG (input = original + uniform noise 0-0.18 mV)
papers.eval_metrics: Bland-Altman agreement of GE 12SL-measured markers (HR, QT, QTcF, QRS duration, PR, P-wave duration, P/R/T amplitudes in II, V1, V5, transition zone); linear-model associations of markers with sex, age, BMI; Cox-model hazard ratios for all-cause mortality; nearest-neighbour re-identification rate in normalized marker space (<=5% limit)
papers.embedding_extractor: GE Marquette 12SL (FDA-cleared) ECG measurement algorithm
papers.notes: Only 3.7% of synthetic ECGs had their source as nearest neighbour (privacy). Preserved QTc sex difference (~9.5 ms) and mortality HRs. PR associations attenuated; MSE loss underweights small P waves. Criticises MSE/Frechet-distance/visual validation as unsuitable; argues for domain-specific markers.
papers.takeaway: Add epidemiological association-preservation tests and marker-space nearest-neighbour re-identification rate to ECGEN-Eval.

papers.title: PG-LRF: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
papers.model_family: FlowMatching (latent rectified flow, PPG-conditioned, physiology-aware VAE-style autoencoder + electro-hemodynamic ODE simulator guidance)
papers.datasets: MC-MED (Stanford ED, 118,385 visits, 70,545 patients; official splits)
papers.loss_functions: PAE: phase-delay consistency (circular squared PAT distance) + L2 reconstruction + beta*KL + global posterior alignment + bidirectional InfoNCE contrastive (instance) + cross-modal decodability L2; Flow: rectified-flow velocity MSE + simulator-guided Euler residual losses on ECG and induced PPG; simulator fitting: waveform + derivative + peak-alignment losses
papers.eval_metrics: MAE; RMSE; FD; FID; heart-rate MAE; fiducial MAE for PR, QRS, QT, QTcF, ST-J60 deviation, P-wave duration, T-wave duration (ms); downstream multi-label CVD detection AUROC (ICD I48, I71, I70, I44, I25, I50) and macro-AUROC; mean±SD over 3 runs
papers.notes: vs PPGFlowECG: MAE 0.87->0.71, FID 44.17->37.79, HR MAE 7.08->3.94; PR error 59.9 ms, QT 29.3 ms. Macro-AUROC 0.633 vs PPG baseline 0.545. Large interval errors even for SOTA show limits of PPG2ECG.
papers.takeaway: Fiducial-interval MAE panel (PR, QRS, QT, QTcF, ST-J60, P, T durations) and HR MAE map directly to ECGEN-Eval features module.

papers.title: PPG-to-ECG Signal Translation for Continuous Atrial Fibrillation Detection via Attention-based Deep State-Space Modeling
papers.model_family: SSM (attention-based deep state-space model, conditional variational / deep Kalman-style latent model)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III Waveform Matched Subset (55 subjects: 43 healthy, 12 AF)
papers.loss_functions: Conditional variational lower bound (ELBO): emission reconstruction log-likelihood − β·KL(posterior || PPG-conditioned prior) at each timestep
papers.eval_metrics: Pearson correlation; RMSE (mV); SNR (dB); AF detection ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, F1 (MINA classifier trained on real ECG, tested on translated)
papers.notes: ρ 0.858/RMSE 0.07/SNR 15.4 dB clean; 0.847/0.076/13.9 under baseline+Gaussian noise. AF PR-AUC 0.986 vs 0.987 real. Probabilistic model provides uncertainty bands for translated ECG.
papers.takeaway: Robustness-to-input-noise evaluation and uncertainty for paired translation; train-on-real/test-on-synthetic for classifier compatibility.

papers.title: PPGFlowECG: Latent Rectified Flow with Cross-Modal Encoding for PPG-Guided ECG Generation and Cardiovascular Disease Detection
papers.model_family: FlowMatching (latent rectified flow, Transformer velocity field with cross-attention; CardioAlign VAE-style cross-modal encoder)
papers.datasets: MCMED; MIMIC-AFib; VitalDB; BIDMC
papers.loss_functions: Stage 1 CardioAlign: Global Distribution Alignment (L2 mean + symmetric KL), Local Instance Discrimination (InfoNCE contrastive), Semantic Decodability Constraint (cross-modal L2 reconstruction), plus waveform reconstruction; Stage 2: rectified-flow MSE velocity loss
papers.eval_metrics: MAE; RMSE; MAE of heart rate (MAEHR, Hamilton detector); downstream per-class AUROC and Macro-AUROC (MCMED multi-label CVD); AF accuracy and F1 (MIMIC-AFib, internal/external); saliency/attribution map comparison; clinical Turing test (5 cardiologists, 100 signals); cardiologist AF diagnosis with PPG only vs PPG+real vs PPG+synthetic ECG; sampling-step ablation
papers.notes: MCMED: MAE 0.73, RMSE 1.14, MAEHR 1.80; Macro-AUROC 63.1. Turing test near chance (0.50; one expert 0.65). Cardiologist AF accuracy with synthetic ECG 0.87 vs real 0.89. Subject-level splits. Baselines incl. CardioGAN, RDDM.
papers.takeaway: Expert 'diagnostic-utility' reader study (real vs synthetic as diagnostic aid) is a strong protocol beyond Turing tests.

papers.title: Principal component conditional generative adversarial networks for imbalanced ECG classification enhancement
papers.model_family: GAN (PCA-based conditional GAN with Transformer encoder-decoder, 'PCA-CGAN')
papers.task: class-cond / augmentation (imbalanced arrhythmia, generates PCA components)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (43 patients)
papers.loss_functions: WGAN-GP (λ=10) + L1/L2; encoder-decoder PCA reconstruction MSE
papers.eval_metrics: NPRD, NRMSE, NMAE (amplitude-range-normalized PRD/RMSE/MAE); leave-one-out and 5-fold CV; Wasserstein distance; Jensen-Shannon divergence; 2-sample KS test p-value; principal component retention rate; frequency-domain correlation coefficient; morphological similarity; downstream ResNet/other Precision, Recall, F1
papers.embedding_extractor: PCA (principal component space)
papers.notes: Explicit critique: RMSE/MAE/PRD are 'diluted' by many steady-state samples and depend on sampling rate; proposes range-normalized NPRD/NRMSE/NMAE. Also uses classifier-feedback sample filtering (keep samples only if metrics improve) - leakage risk.
papers.takeaway: Adopt range-normalized NRMSE/NPRD/NMAE and consider QRS-weighted errors to counter dilution by isoelectric segments.

papers.title: Quantum-Refined Latent Diffusion: A Hybrid Generative Framework for Imbalanced ECG Classification
papers.model_family: Hybrid (latent diffusion: spectral-guided cVAE + class-conditional latent DDPM with CFG + Quantum Latent Refinement via parameterized quantum circuits)
papers.task: augmentation (class-cond minority beats S, V, F)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (44 records, AAMI classes; intra-patient temporal 80/10/10 split)
papers.loss_functions: cVAE: MSE + L1 DFT-magnitude spectral loss + β-annealed KL (β→0.05); latent DDPM: noise-prediction MSE; QLR: stay loss ||z_refined − z_raw||² + MMD² (median-heuristic RBF) to real class latent bank; classifier: class-weighted CE
papers.eval_metrics: Macro F1 (primary); per-class precision/recall; accuracy; paired t-test over 5 seeds; class-mean waveform RMSD, max |Δ|, cosine similarity; latent distribution drift = multi-bandwidth (5 RBF kernels) MMD²; PCA/KDE latent plots
papers.embedding_extractor: cVAE latent space (32-d) for MMD
papers.notes: Macro F1 0.747 baseline → up to 0.835 with augmentation. Fidelity measured only on class-mean waveforms (cosine sim misleading for multimodal V class, authors note). Intra-patient temporal split means same patients appear in train and test. MMD used both as training loss and eval metric (circularity risk).
papers.takeaway: Use multi-bandwidth MMD rather than single kernel; avoid evaluating with the same metric used as training loss; mean-waveform similarity hides diversity.

papers.title: Reconstructing 12-Lead ECG from 3-Lead ECG using Variational Autoencoder to Improve Cardiac Disease Detection of Wearable ECG Devices
papers.model_family: VAE (WearECG: conditional VAE with residual conv blocks / attention, KL-regularized latent)
papers.task: lead-reconstruction (12-lead from 3 leads, e.g. II, V1, V5)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (training/validation); PTB-XL (downstream generalization)
papers.loss_functions: ELBO: MSE reconstruction + beta * KL (beta = 1e-4); optional perceptual loss from pretrained ECG encoder
papers.eval_metrics: MSE; MAE (per lead and overall); FID on ECGFounder features; downstream AUROC/sensitivity/specificity with frozen ECGFounder + head trained on synthetic ECGs (~40 conditions; regional MI); blinded Turing test with 3 cardiologists; physician MI detection/localization on generated ECGs (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1)
papers.embedding_extractor: ECGFounder (pretrained on >10M ECGs) for FID and downstream classification
papers.notes: MSE 0.00100, MAE 0.01782, FID 12.64. Cardiologist Turing test accuracies 52/44/44% on 50 samples (chance level). Synthetic-trained head macro-AUROC 0.8333 MIMIC; regional MI 0.8764. Text mixes up MAE/MSE values (inconsistent labeling) and mentions MIMIC-III in data statement.
papers.takeaway: FID on ECGFounder features (as in our FED) plus foundation-model TSTR and Turing test is a complete protocol.

papers.title: Region-Disentangled Diffusion Model for High-Fidelity PPG-to-ECG Translation
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.model_family: Diffusion (RDDM: region-disentangled DDPM with ROI (QRS)-guided forward process, two denoisers)
papers.datasets: WESAD; DALIA; CAPNO; BIDMC; MIMIC-AFib (training); CardioBench: WESAD, DALIA, MIMIC-AFib, PPG-BP, Cuffless-BP
papers.loss_functions: lambda1*||mu*eps - eps_theta(x_t^m,c,t)||^2 (ROI/QRS noise) + lambda2*||x_t^m - rho_phi(x_t,c,t)||^2 (non-ROI denoising)
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; Fréchet Distance (FD, following CardioGAN); CardioBench: HR estimation MAE (bpm, Hamilton detector), AFib detection F1/accuracy, stress and affect classification F1/accuracy, diabetes detection, SBP/DBP estimation MAE (train on real, test on generated)
papers.notes: Introduces CardioBench: train-on-real/test-on-generated downstream benchmark with real-test performance as upper bound. Only 10 sampling steps. Subject-independent evaluation.
papers.takeaway: TRTS downstream benchmark with real-data upper bound and HR-MAE are useful; clarify FD (curve) vs FID-style naming.

papers.title: ReHeartNet: Reconstruct Electrocardiogram From Photoplethysmography by Using Dense Connected Deep Learning Model
papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology
papers.model_family: Other (deterministic regression: densely connected BiLSTM, DC-BiLSTM); baselines GAN (CardioGAN), BiLSTM, Transformer
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III; BIDMC; TBME-RR; CBIC-Heart (new long-term dataset)
papers.fs_hz: varies per dataset (not unified in text)
papers.loss_functions: RMSE reconstruction loss
