papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; Pearson correlation r; beat-timing error (mean absolute R-peak displacement, Pan-Tompkins, nearest-peak matching without tolerance window); 95% CIs across subjects; significance tests vs baselines
papers.notes: Introduces beat-timing error since amplitude metrics miss R-peak displacement critical for HR/HRV. Cross-dataset sampling-rate differences used to test robustness.
papers.takeaway: Add an R-peak beat-timing error metric for paired reconstruction tasks.

papers.title: Shape and amplitude decoupling in pulsatile physiological signal synthesis and its evaluation
authors: Kim J, Park K, Chen L, Kim K.
papers.model_family: VAE (VABAM: variational framework with cascaded HPF/LPF filtering, bidirectional GRU, Gaussian shape latent z + uniform amplitude parameter theta); baselines ConVAE, FactorVAE, TCVAE, VDVAE, DiffWave, VDWave, WaveNet
papers.task: other (amplitude-controllable synthesis with shape-amplitude decoupling; frequency-cutoff conditioning)
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III Waveform (ABP and ECG); VitalDB (ABP and ECG); cross-dataset train/test
papers.loss_functions: ELBO with four terms: signal reconstruction log p(y|x); feature-subset reconstruction log p(x|z,theta) vs q(x|y,theta); KL(q(z|y)||N(0,I)); KL(q(theta|y)||Uniform) relaxed via reparameterized Bernoulli
papers.eval_metrics: Five metrics: waveform shape factorization (SF), shape preservation / spectral distortion (SP/SD), amplitude modulation controllability (AC), spectral similarity (via conditional mutual information / KL on PSD permutation densities using FFT, DCT, Welch), reconstruction R2; composite ISCORE (arithmetic/geometric/harmonic mean of normalized metrics, Linfoot informational correlation normalisation)
papers.notes: Nature Communications evaluation-oriented paper: introduces CMI-based PSD metrics and an aggregate ISCORE; shows ranking depends on PSD estimator (FFT/DCT/Welch) and aggregation mean, so they report all. SF excluded for non-factorized models (diffusion). 400k/50k/20k train/val/test per signal/dataset.
papers.takeaway: Report spectral metrics under multiple PSD estimators and justify any composite score (AM/GM/HM sensitivity).

papers.title: Simulator and Experience Enhanced Diffusion Model for Comprehensive ECG Generation
papers.model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM in VAE latent space, ODE-simulator-enhanced, LLM-powered EHR retrieval; 'SE-Diff')
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (800,035 ECGs); MIMIC-IV-Clinical (EHR retrieval)
papers.loss_functions: VAE: full reconstruction + β-KL + beat-decoder loss + log-spectrum (rFFT) band-weighted spectral loss; Diffusion: L_DDPM + λ simulator-guided Euler ODE-consistency loss + γ inter-lead (Einthoven/Goldberger) consistency loss
papers.eval_metrics: Per-lead MAE; NRMSE; Pearson r; HR MAE (MAE_HR); relative CLIP score (rCLIP = s(gen,text)/s(real,text)); relative FID (rFID = FID(gen,real)/FID(real split1, real split2)) in ECG embedding space; downstream F1, Accuracy, AUROC for imbalanced sex and SVT classification
papers.embedding_extractor: ECG encoder of a CLIP-style ECG-text model (specific model not named)
papers.notes: Normalising FID and CLIP by real-vs-real reference values controls for encoder bias - a good practice. Physics losses include Einthoven/Goldberger inter-lead identity constraints. Only baseline is DiffuSETS.
papers.takeaway: Implement rFID (FID normalised by real-split FID) and inter-lead Einthoven/Goldberger residual metrics; rCLIP for text-conditioned models.

papers.title: Single-Lead ECG Arrhythmia Classification Based on Peak-Enhanced Attention Network and Quality-Aware GAN Data Augmentation Framework
papers.model_family: GAN (Quality-Aware GAN, QA-GAN: CNN + BiLSTM, kurtosis-based dynamic soft-label discriminator)
papers.datasets: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2017 (AliveCor, 8,528 recordings); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (classifier adaptability)
papers.loss_functions: Generator: standard adversarial loss; Discriminator: dynamic soft-label BCE with real-sample target y = α + (1−α)·tanh(log(K(x)+1)/5) from signal kurtosis K (α=0.7 best)
papers.eval_metrics: visual comparison; t-SNE overlap of real vs synthetic AF features; downstream classifier precision, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, F1, macro-F1, AUC/ROC, PR curves; comparison vs SMOTE, random oversampling, class-weighted loss; noise robustness
papers.embedding_extractor: not specified (t-SNE on signal features)
papers.notes: Generator quality evaluated only visually and via downstream augmentation (F1 0.793 baseline → 0.816 with QA-GAN vs 0.809 class-weighted loss). Kurtosis used as a signal-quality index during training — could also serve as an SQI metric for synthetic ECGs.
papers.takeaway: Kurtosis-based SQI is a cheap reference-free quality metric; also shows need to compare augmentation against SMOTE/class-weighting baselines.

papers.title: Spatially-Conditioned Variational Autoencoder with Latent Manifold Harvesting for High-Fidelity 12-Lead ECG Synthesis
papers.model_family: VAE (spatially-conditioned cVAE with multi-resolution beat-position mask injection, nearest-neighbour upsampling; Latent Manifold Harvesting latent bank)
papers.task: class-cond (major pathology + comorbidity profile; beat-position mask)
papers.datasets: Large 12-lead ECG database v1.0.0 (Chapman-Shaoxing/Ningbo, 45,152 patients, SNOMED-CT codes)
papers.loss_functions: MSE reconstruction + KL divergence (standard VAE ELBO)
papers.eval_metrics: visual side-by-side inspection; per-channel 1D-ResNet ensemble classifier applied to synthetic ECGs: Pearson correlation between predicted pathology prevalence and training distribution ('Ensemble Correlation'); Cumulative Mean Certainty / Reliability Score (mean |p-0.5|*2); reconstruction MSE; heuristic peak-alignment acceptance criteria
papers.embedding_extractor: per-channel 1D-ResNet classifiers trained on real data
papers.notes: Latent Manifold Harvesting: only latents whose decodings pass R-peak count/location/amplitude and baseline-smoothness tolerance are banked, then jittered (rejection sampling biases diversity). Per-lead independent VAEs ignore inter-lead consistency. Ensemble correlation r>=0.98 for AFIB, LBBB, AF; 100 samples per pathology; CPU-only training.
papers.takeaway: Classifier label-prevalence correlation and confidence are cheap conditional-fidelity checks; peak-alignment heuristics could serve as a plausibility metric.

papers.title: SSSD-ECG-nle: New Label Embeddings with Structured State-Space Models for ECG generation
papers.model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG with new label embeddings 'nle': separate embeddings for label presence/absence; S4 backbone)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (folds 1-8 train, 9 val, 10 test)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE
papers.eval_metrics: TSTR and TRTS with xResNet1d50 (binary per pathology: AFIB, CRBBB, PVC, 1AVB, CLBBB): G-mean, F1-score; multilabel TSTR/TRTS weighted G-mean, F1, ROC-AUC; real-data augmentation with synthetic positives; convergence analysis over training checkpoints; physician evaluation: text-report diagnosis accuracy on 100 real + 100 synthetic, and direct real-vs-synthetic discrimination (380 ECGs) confusion matrix
papers.code: https://github.com/ispras/EcgLib (synthetic data and physician evaluations released)
papers.notes: Key pitfall: good TSTR yet physicians identified synthetic ECGs almost perfectly (279/280 synthetic, 99/100 real correct); cues were low voltage, apparently reversed chest electrodes, artefacts. Authors dropped relation metrics (DTW, MMD, Wasserstein) and TSTS as 'uninformative'.
papers.takeaway: TSTR alone is insufficient; add realism detectors (low-voltage, lead-reversal/inter-lead consistency checks) and a real-vs-synthetic classifier score.

papers.title: Style translation of simulated ECGs to realistic ECGs with generative adversarial networks for data-scarce clinical settings: challenges and opportunities
papers.model_family: GAN (CycleGAN style transfer simulated->realistic ECG)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (987 ECGs, 56 RBBB); MedalCareXL simulations (25 RBBB)
papers.loss_functions: CycleGAN adversarial + cycle-consistency (implied by CycleGAN; not detailed)
papers.eval_metrics: Downstream RBBB classifier AUC; average precision (AP) for real-only, real+raw simulations, real+translated simulations
papers.notes: Conference abstract. Raw simulations harmed (AUC 0.93, AP 0.68); translated restored to baseline (AUC 0.95 vs 0.96, AP 0.81 vs 0.79). Notes clinicians recognise synthetic style; argues diffusion models offer objective convergence diagnostics vs unstable GANs.
papers.takeaway: Report the 'harm' case: augmentation can degrade utility; include real-only baseline and AP for rare classes.

papers.title: Synthetic artificial intelligence in cardiology: from generative models to clinical applications
papers.model_family: Survey (GANs, VAEs, Diffusion, Transformers, Autoregressive models, Digital Twins, Synthetic Cohort Simulators in cardiology)
papers.datasets: not applicable (mentions synthetic 12-lead ECG from electrophysiological simulations, DeepFake ECG)
papers.loss_functions: described conceptually only: adversarial training (generator vs discriminator); variational/probabilistic latent modelling; progressive denoising (diffusion)
papers.eval_metrics: no specific quantitative metric catalogue; calls for standardized evaluation frameworks, clinical relevance validation, traceability/auditing, clinician validation of realism, logical consistency and population representativeness (TIMA framework: coverage, novelty, coherence); privacy preservation; bias/under-representation checks
papers.embedding_extractor: not applicable
papers.notes: Clinician-oriented state-of-the-art review (Eur Heart J Open). Identifies lack of standardized evaluation frameworks and labelling as a key risk; recommends embedding clinicians in validation (TIMA). ECG coverage is brief; few concrete metrics.
papers.takeaway: Supports including expert-review and bias/representativeness reporting in ECGEN-Eval reports; little metric-specific detail.

papers.title: Synthetic Data Generation via Generative Adversarial Networks in Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Image- and Signal-Based Studies
papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology
papers.model_family: Survey (GANs in healthcare, image and signal; PRISMA, 72 studies)
papers.datasets: catalogued: various (MRI, CT, ECG incl. MIT-BIH, PTB-XL etc.)
papers.loss_functions: Catalogues GAN architectures (cGAN 31%, CycleGAN 18%, Pix2Pix, StyleGAN, PGGAN, SynSigGAN, DC-WGAN); minimax adversarial and cycle-consistency losses
papers.eval_metrics: Catalogued: PSNR; SSIM; MAE; FID; Dice; NMSE; RMSE; AUC; accuracy/sensitivity/specificity; image Turing test
papers.notes: Signal section is thin (ECG: SynSigGAN low FID/RMSE; SSSD-ECG high AUC). Main finding: no standardized metrics, SSIM/PSNR miss clinical significance; recommends no-reference metrics usable also as losses.
papers.takeaway: Supports need for clinically grounded, standardized, ideally no-reference metrics.

papers.title: Synthetic ECG Generation for Data Augmentation and Transfer Learning in Arrhythmia Classification
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DiffWave/SSSD-ECG; Time-Diffusion = HF Diffusers Unet1D conditional) + VQ-VAE/MaskGIT (Time-VQVAE, TimeVQVAE)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL; Chapman-Shaoxing; merged PTB-XL+Chapman (7 rhythm classes: SBRAD, SR, AFIB, STACH, AFLT, SARRH, SVTAC)
papers.loss_functions: not detailed; uses original models' objectives (DiffWave variational bound / diffusion noise prediction; VQ-VAE + MaskGIT prior)
papers.eval_metrics: t-SNE, UMAP, PaCMAP visualisations; 2-sample classifier test (real-vs-synthetic accuracy, 50% ideal); MMD (RBF); TrRTeR, TrSTeS, TrSTeR (TSTR), TrRTeS (TRTS), TrRSTeR (augmentation) with accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC (n=25 repeats); fine-tuning transferability with 20-80% real data
papers.notes: Key criticism: MMD and t-SNE/UMAP visualisations failed to distinguish synthetic from real, while classifier-based tests (2-sample test, TSTR/TRTS) revealed clear differences. Augmentation gains negligible per dataset, positive on merged set. Time-VQVAE best for fine-tuning but still below real-only.
papers.takeaway: Add a classifier two-sample test (C2ST) and full TrRTeR/TSTR/TRTS/TrRSTeR matrix; MMD alone is underpowered.

papers.title: Synthetic ECG signal generation using generative neural networks
papers.model_family: GAN (comparison of 5 models: Classic FC GAN, DC-DC GAN, BiLSTM-DC GAN, AE/VAE-DC GAN hybrid, WGAN)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (Normal beats, lead I; N vs LBBB for augmentation test)
papers.loss_functions: Binary cross-entropy adversarial loss (all models); AE/VAE-DC GAN: weighted sum of adversarial loss + L1 reconstruction loss; WGAN loss for WGAN model
papers.eval_metrics: DTW, Frechet and Euclidean distances to template; Method 1 mean all-pairs set distance; Method 2/3 distances to random or expert-selected template (min distance); Method 4 productivity rate (% accepted beats under distance threshold); Method 5 expert visual inspection; ResNet34 augmentation precision/recall/F1/accuracy and confusion matrices
papers.notes: Introduces threshold, accepted beat, productivity rate concepts. Euclidean distance unsuitable: a beat with minimum Euclidean distance lacked all morphological features. DTW and discrete Frechet agree; Frechet is a true metric. Classic GAN 72.3% productivity (DTW). Template choice (SAB vs expert-picked) affects scores. Includes table of prior ECG-GAN metrics.
papers.takeaway: Acceptance/productivity rate under a DTW threshold is a practical metric; avoid plain Euclidean for morphology.

papers.title: Synthetic Electrocardiogram Spectrogram Generation Using Generative Adversarial Network‐Based Models: A Comparative Study
papers.model_family: GAN (DCGAN, conditional GAN, WGAN-GP) on 2-D spectrogram images
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (N, L, R, V, A beats grouped into normal/abnormal)
papers.loss_functions: DCGAN: binary cross-entropy adversarial; CGAN: conditional cross-entropy adversarial; WGAN-GP: Wasserstein critic loss + lambda gradient penalty
papers.eval_metrics: FID (Inception-V3 'pre-aux' 768-d layer via pytorch-fid); intra-class SSIM diversity (average/max/min pairwise SSIM among generated, values near 1 = mode collapse); training runtime and GPU memory; downstream 2D-CNN precision, recall, F1, accuracy on GAN-balanced vs imbalanced training sets
papers.embedding_extractor: Inception-V3 (ImageNet), 'pre-aux' 768-d layer
papers.notes: Explicit pitfall: pool_3 FID needs >2048 samples (else complex/NaN covariance); switching layer makes FID values non-comparable across works. Pairwise SSIM among synthetic samples used as mode-collapse/diversity detector.
papers.takeaway: Add an intra-set pairwise-similarity diversity score (mode-collapse flag) and warn when sample count < embedding dim in Fréchet metrics.

papers.title: Synthetic electrocardiograms for Brugada syndrome: from data generation to expert cardiologists evaluation
papers.model_family: GAN (Pulse2Pulse)
papers.task: evaluation (expert Turing test of class-specific synthetic ECGs)
papers.datasets: Private: 12-lead ECGs from 21 Brugada syndrome patients (5-min recordings)
papers.loss_functions: not reported (refers to Pulse2Pulse paper)
papers.eval_metrics: Expert visual Turing test by 7 Brugada specialists (>15 y): accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 (real=positive); two rounds ≥2 h apart; Wilcoxon signed-rank; intra-rater Cohen's kappa
papers.notes: Experts at chance or worse: accuracy 40%/42%, specificity 22%/26%, sensitivity 58%; kappa −0.12 to 0.80. Bias toward calling ECGs real. Same display settings (25 mm/s, 10 mm/mV). Raises disclosure/watermarking concerns.
papers.takeaway: Expert Turing-test protocol (blinded, repeated rounds, kappa) is a template; report specificity separately since raters are biased to 'real'.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware PPG-2-ECG for Enhanced Cardiovascular Diagnosis using Diffusion Models
papers.model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM-style denoiser for PPG->ECG; reverse ECG->PPG model for data completion); UA-P2E uncertainty-aware classification
papers.datasets: MIMIC-III matched waveform (PPG-ECG pairs); PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (11 lead-II-detectable conditions, with synthesized PPG)
papers.loss_functions: diffusion noise-prediction (denoiser epsilon(X_t,Y,t)); classifier cross-entropy
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE (single sample and MMSE/mean of K=100 samples); Frechet Distance (1-FD single sample, 100-FD multi-sample); ROC/AUROC of classification strategies; risk-coverage curves for selective classification; conformal calibration guarantees; MSE and PSNR training curves; pairwise synthetic ECG distances
papers.notes: Key insight: averaging posterior samples approximates MMSE estimator, giving low RMSE but worse perceptual quality; individual samples have higher RMSE (perception-distortion trade-off, Blau & Michaeli). Diagnosis uses expected score over many ECG samples; uncertainty via sample variability; compared to CardioGAN, RDDM.
papers.takeaway: For stochastic generators, report both per-sample and mean-of-samples distortion plus distributional metrics (perception-distortion trade-off).

papers.title: UniECG: Understanding and Generating ECG in One Unified Model
papers.model_family: LLM (unified multimodal LLM with special ECG tokens mapped to frozen DiffuSETS text-conditioned latent diffusion; 'UniECG')
papers.datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (737,875 training; 10,000 held-out eval); GEM test set (2,381) for explanation
papers.loss_functions: Weighted NLL for ECG_START/ECG token emission (L_e) + MSE between mapper output and frozen DiffuSETS text embedding (L_d)
papers.eval_metrics: FID; Precision; Recall; F1 (signal-level, precision/recall-based); HR MAE; CLIP score (ECG-text); generation success rate; explanation scored by LLM judge (GLM-5) under ECG-R1 rubric
papers.embedding_extractor: DiffuSETS evaluation protocol embeddings (specific encoder not named in text)
papers.notes: Signal-, feature- and diagnostic-level metric hierarchy. UniECG vs DiffuSETS: FID 79.43 vs 25.26, recall 0.615 vs 0.709 while precision ~equal (0.939 vs 0.941) - shows precision/recall separates fidelity from coverage. 95.61% decoding success rate.
papers.takeaway: Report precision/recall alongside FID to separate realism from coverage; 'generation success rate' for LLM-driven generators.

papers.title: Variational autoencoder–based neural electrocardiogram synthesis trained by FEM-based heart simulator
papers.model_family: VAE (conditional VAE, fully connected encoder/decoder) trained on FEM simulator output (surrogate model)
papers.task: other (parameter-conditioned 12-lead ECG synthesis from 16 cardiac parameters; simulator surrogate)
papers.datasets: UT-Heart FEM multi-physics simulator dataset (2,880 ECG variations)
papers.loss_functions: conditional VAE ELBO (reconstruction log-likelihood + KL divergence)
papers.eval_metrics: Position Mean Absolute Error (PMAE) of Q, R, S, T fiducial positions vs ground truth; PSNR per lead; dependence of errors on cardiac parameter values (significance tests)
papers.notes: Paired evaluation against simulator ground truth; PSNR ~55-65 dB (very high because simulated noise-free signals). PMAE excludes P wave and outlier positions (>100/150 ms). Notes that appropriate metric depends on purpose (e.g. periodicity-focused for arrhythmia). Synthesis takes seconds on a laptop vs supercomputer hours.
papers.takeaway: Fiducial-point position error (Q/R/S/T PMAE) is a clinically interpretable paired metric worth adding for conditional/paired tasks.

papers.title: Versatile Cardiovascular Signal Generation with a Unified Diffusion Transformer
papers.model_family: Diffusion (UniCardio: multi-modal diffusion transformer, noise-prediction, continual learning over modality combinations)
papers.task: PPG2ECG / other-modality2ECG; imputation; denoising (also PPG/ECG->BP translation)
papers.datasets: Cuffless BP dataset (pretraining, 339 h ICU PPG/ECG/BP); PTB-XL (ST change, hypertrophy); MIMIC PERform AF; WESAD (HR); MIMIC (SBP/DBP)
papers.loss_functions: Diffusion noise-prediction (epsilon) MSE loss, with continual-learning phases balancing modality combinations
papers.eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; Min-RMSE and Min-MAE (minimum over bounded temporal shifts); KS-test statistic; SNR (supplement); RMSE ratio for ablations; downstream accuracy, sensitivity, specificity for ST change, hypertrophy, AF detection; heart-rate MAE; SBP/DBP MAE; clinician assessment by two cardiologists (third for disagreement); inference time
papers.code: https://github.com/thu-ml/UniCardio (to be released; code in supplementary materials)
papers.notes: Min-RMSE/Min-MAE over small time shifts tolerate misalignment that inflates pointwise errors - useful pitfall fix. Generated signals evaluated as substitutes for ground truth in diagnosis/vital-sign estimation, including unseen domains. Sample-entropy filtering of training data. Random 80/10/10 segment split (possible subject leakage on pretraining set).
papers.takeaway: Adopt shift-tolerant (min over lags) RMSE/MAE for paired tasks and task-substitution utility tests.

papers.title: SynSigGAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Synthetic Biomedical Signal Generation
papers.model_family: GAN (SynSigGAN: bidirectional Grid-LSTM generator + CNN discriminator)
papers.task: unconditional / class-wise (per-annotation segments) synthesis of ECG, EEG, EMG, PPG
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (ECG); Siena Scalp EEG; Sleep-EDF (EMG); BIDMC PPG and Respiration
papers.loss_functions: standard GAN generator/discriminator adversarial losses (DWT-based denoising in preprocessing evaluated with SNR, RMSE, PRD)
papers.eval_metrics: Pearson correlation coefficient (mean); MAE; RMSE; PRD; Fréchet distance (discrete curve distance); classification accuracy of other models on synthetic signals; SNR/RMSE/PRD for preprocessing denoising
papers.notes: ECG: PCC 0.9991, MAE 0.218, RMSE 0.126, PRD 6.343, FD 0.936; baselines PRD 68-119. Established the PCC/MAE/RMSE/PRD/FD 'paired' metric suite later copied widely; pairing of generated vs original signals is not clearly defined for unconditional generation.
papers.takeaway: Classic metric suite origin; ECGEN-Eval should implement curve FD and PRD with explicit nearest-neighbour pairing and document the caveat.

papers.title: DeepFake electrocardiograms using generative adversarial networks are the beginning of the end for privacy issues in medicine
papers.model_family: GAN (WaveGAN* and Pulse2Pulse U-Net generator, WGAN-GP)
papers.datasets: GESUS; Inter99 (Danish population studies; MUSE 12SL 'Normal' ECGs only)
papers.loss_functions: WGAN-GP (gradient penalty), 5 critic updates per generator update
papers.eval_metrics: Fraction of synthetic ECGs classified 'Normal' by commercial GE MUSE 12SL algorithm (model selection across epochs); distributions of MUSE-measured HR, P duration, QT, QRS, PR, STJ/R/T amplitudes vs real; QT-RR correlation preservation; covariance structures
papers.embedding_extractor: commercial ECG interpretation program (GE MUSE 12SL) as measurement/diagnostic oracle
papers.notes: 150,000 DeepFake ECGs released; 81.3% classified Normal. Clinical-parameter distributions matched; truncation of HR at clinical boundaries discussed. Privacy claimed but not quantitatively tested (no memorization/MIA).
papers.takeaway: Use an external ECG interpretation program as an oracle: % plausible/diagnosis-consistent plus clinical-parameter distribution and covariance (e.g., QT-RR) comparison.

papers.title: Synthetic ECG Signal Generation Using Probabilistic Diffusion Models
papers.model_family: Diffusion (Improved DDPM on 2D GASF/GADF/MTF image embeddings of beats) vs GAN (WGAN-GP)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII; N class for generation, L class for authenticity test)
papers.loss_functions: Improved DDPM hybrid loss L_hybrid = L_simple + lambda L_vlb (cosine schedule); WGAN-GP (Wasserstein + gradient penalty)
papers.eval_metrics: Average DTW distance; average Frechet distance (quality vs real reference rl-rl); MMD^2 (linear kernel, 7000 vs 7000; real-vs-real reference); authenticity test: ResNet34 N vs L classifier trained on imbalanced set augmented with synthetic beats, reporting accuracy, precision, recall, ROC AUC, average precision, PR-AUC
papers.notes: WGAN-GP beat DDPM on all metrics (DTW 2.12 vs 6.36-6.95; MMD 1.0 vs 35.9-44). Good practice: real-vs-real reference values (DTW 2.09, FD 0.718, MMD 0) as baseline floor. 'Authenticity' here means augmentation utility, not privacy. 2D embedding then de-embedding may hurt diffusion.
papers.takeaway: Always report real-vs-real reference values (split-half) for each metric to calibrate what 'good' means.

papers.title: Diffusion-based conditional ECG generation with structured state space models
papers.model_family: Diffusion (DDPM with structured state space S4 backbone, 'SSSD-ECG'); baselines WaveGAN*, Pulse2Pulse
papers.datasets: PTB-XL
papers.n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 reconstructed from limb-lead relations)
papers.loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction L2 loss (class-conditional)
papers.eval_metrics: Classifier-based measures with XResNet1d50 macro AUROC over 71 labels: Train-synthetic/Test-real (TSTR), Train-real/Test-synthetic (TRTS) via fixed reference classifier, Train-synth/Test-synth internal consistency; qualitative beat-level quantile-band plots; conditional label interpolation; clinical Turing test with a cardiologist (44 ECGs, real vs synthetic + diagnosis)
papers.embedding_extractor: pretrained ECG classifier (XResNet1d50 trained on real PTB-XL) used as reference classifier
papers.code: https://github.com/AI4HealthUOL/SSSD-ECG (cited as AI4HealthUOL/SSSD-ECG; synthetic PTB-XL copy also released)
papers.notes: AUROC: real 0.9317; SSSD TSTR 0.8402 vs Pulse2Pulse 0.5968, WaveGAN* 0.5816; TRTS 0.9434. Train-synth/test-synth near 0.98-0.995 for all - uninformative. Abandoned alpha-precision/beta-recall due to unstable one-class embeddings. Turing test: cardiologist misdiagnosed 43%, near-chance real/synthetic discrimination.
papers.takeaway: Adopt the TSTR/TRTS/TSTS triad with a fixed reference classifier; note TSTS is uninformative.

papers.title: ME-GAN: Learning Panoptic Electrocardio Representations for Multi-view ECG Synthesis Conditioned on Heart Diseases
papers.model_family: GAN (ME-GAN: two-stage generator with Nef-Net decoder, MixNorm disease conditioning; LSGAN + ACGAN-style major discriminator + view discriminator)
papers.datasets: Tianchi ECG (31,779 records, 500 Hz; LAD, RAD, RBBB); PTB (549 records, 1000 Hz)
papers.loss_functions: LSGAN least-squares adversarial loss (a=1, b=0) + auxiliary disease classification CE/BCE (ACGAN-style) + view-discriminator MSE angle-regression adversarial loss (view-consistency)
papers.eval_metrics: relative FID (rFID = FID(gen, X2)/FID(X1, X2), real-real split as normaliser); 1-NN classifier accuracy (1NNC two-sample test); augmentation PR-AUC with 1D ResNet-34; pairwise distance among views within same case vs real baseline; rFID sensitivity to noise/line-segment/blur perturbations
papers.embedding_extractor: 1D Inception pretrained on ImageNet images reshaped to 12x512 (not an ECG model)
papers.notes: Proposes rFID to normalise image-pretrained-feature FID by a real-vs-real FID; validated monotone response to noise, blur, line-segment perturbations; real-real denominator std 0.212 on PTB. Baseline augmentation PR-AUC 0.879. Feature extractor not ECG-trained — a known weakness later addressed by ECG foundation-model FED.
papers.takeaway: Report FD/FED alongside a real-vs-real reference (ratio, as in rFID) and add 1-NN two-sample accuracy; view/lead-consistency distance is a useful multi-lead metric.

papers.title: Deep Generative Models for Physiological Signals: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.model_family: Survey (systematic review of GANs, VAEs, diffusion models for ECG, EEG, PPG, EMG)
papers.datasets: review of 71 studies (55 + 16 expert-added; 2018-2023); most-used datasets include MIT-BIH, PTB/PTB-XL, BIDMC, DEAP, Sleep-EDF
papers.loss_functions: Catalogued: GAN cross-entropy adversarial loss; WGAN / WGAN-GP for stability; LSGAN least-squares loss; SeqGAN policy-gradient (RL) training; VAE reconstruction + KL regularization (trade-off discussed); diffusion denoising objectives
papers.eval_metrics: Augmentation: ED, DTW, PCC, KLD, RMSE, PRD, MAE, FD, KMMD, relative entropy, TWED, Soft-DTW, MMD, multivariate DTW, MSE, EMD, IS, FID, Wasserstein distance, Chamfer distance, JSD, SSIM, cross-correlation, NRMSE; Denoising: SNR, SNRimp, PRD, MSE, RMSE, SSD, MAD, mean correlation, PPE, cosine similarity; Imputation/forecasting: MAPE, RMSE, IS, FID, MAE, CRPS, MSE, CD, EMD, MMD; Modality transfer: MAE, RMSE, PRD, FD, PCC, DTW, HR MAE, Hellinger distance; utility: precision, recall, F1, accuracy, Cohen's kappa; qualitative visual inspection, cardiologist assessment
papers.embedding_extractor: not applicable
papers.notes: >60% of studies rely on visual inspection. Most used metrics: RMSE, MAE, MMD, PRD, DTW, FID. Highlights absence of standardized evaluation protocols and calls for a common protocol; notes lack of reproducible comparisons since code often unavailable.
papers.takeaway: Metric catalogue confirms ECGEN-Eval's core set; consider CRPS for imputation and TWED/Soft-DTW as alternatives.

papers.title: ECG ODE-GAN: Learning Ordinary Differential Equations of ECG Dynamics via Generative Adversarial Learning
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.model_family: GAN (ODE-GAN: generator learns ECG dynamics dh/dt solved with Euler ODE steps; physics-informed with McSharry simulator parameters)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI inter-patient partition; N, S, V, F)
papers.loss_functions: standard cross-entropy adversarial losses (generator and discriminator); baselines DCGAN cross-entropy, WGAN EM distance
papers.eval_metrics: downstream heartbeat classification (1D-ResNet) trained on real + synthetic: per-class precision-recall curves and operating points (Re, Pr) per AAMI standard
papers.notes: Evaluation purely by augmentation benefit (TRTR vs augmented), following SimGAN practice; no direct fidelity or distribution metric. e.g., SVEB (Re 0.40, Pr 0.83) vs SimGAN Pr 0.70. Patient-wise AAMI split.
papers.takeaway: Augmentation-utility with patient-wise AAMI splits and per-class PR curves is the standard beat-level utility protocol.

papers.title: Multivariate Generative Adversarial Networks and Their Loss Functions for Synthesis of Multichannel ECGs
papers.model_family: GAN (MVGAN: 2-layer LSTM generator, 2-D CNN discriminator with minibatch discrimination; DP variant)
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm; MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
papers.loss_functions: Compared losses: LSGAN; LSGAN-DTW (LSGAN with multivariate DTW penalty term); DTWGAN (MVDTW as criterion); Loss-Sensitive GAN (LS-GAN); LS-GAN-DTW; DP via gradient noise (GAN-DP)
papers.eval_metrics: MMD; multivariate dependent DTW (MVDTW); real-vs-synthetic discriminability by SVC and LSTM classifiers (accuracy near 0.5 = good); membership inference attack (presence disclosure precision/recall vs threshold ε); benchmarks vs multivariate VAE and LSTM
papers.notes: LSGAN-DTW best (4.9% over LSGAN on normalised MMD+DTW). MIA: ~0% recall for ε ≤0.4·mean distance; DP version 0% up to 0.5. Early use of classifier two-sample test and MIA for ECG GANs.
papers.takeaway: Add classifier two-sample test (real-vs-synthetic discriminability) and distance-threshold membership inference to the privacy section.

papers.title: Text-to-ECG: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram Synthesis Conditioned on Clinical Text Reports
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
papers.model_family: AR-Transformer (Auto-TTE: VQ-VAE tokenizer + autoregressive Transformer decoder + HiFi-GAN decoder); baselines DDPM-style diffusion on raw 12-lead, Tacotron 2 + Griffin-Lim / HiFi-GAN
papers.task: text-cond (clinical text reports + age/sex patient-specific embedding)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (21,833 text-ECG pairs); private Sejong General Hospital dataset (37,329 pairs)
papers.loss_functions: VQ-VAE: L2 reconstruction + codebook + commitment (stop-gradient) losses; Transformer: token cross-entropy; HiFi-GAN: LS-GAN adversarial (MSD+MPD) + L1 STFT spectrogram loss + L1 discriminator feature-matching loss (weights 1, 2, 45)
papers.eval_metrics: AUROC of ResNet-34 multi-label classifier on samples generated from diagnosis prompts (6 classes); CLIP score (ECG-text contrastive encoder); FID using self-supervised ECG model pretrained on PhysioNet 2021 (64-d features); precision and recall (Kynkaanniemi et al.); cardiologist ranking (3 cardiologists, text-ECG alignment and realism, 100 samples); 10x bootstrap mean/std and t-tests
papers.embedding_extractor: self-supervised ECG model pretrained on PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (last layer modified to 64-d)
papers.notes: Auto-TTE FID 7.17, precision 0.946, recall 0.842; avg AUROC 0.857; CLIP score 0.644. Early text-conditioned ECG work introducing CLIP-style text-ECG alignment score and ECG-FID with SSL encoder; bootstrap + significance testing.
papers.takeaway: Adopt CLIP-style condition-alignment score and bootstrap CIs for FID/precision/recall; document the embedding model.

papers.title: BioDiffusion: A Versatile Diffusion Model for Biomedical Signal Synthesis
papers.model_family: Diffusion (U-Net DDPM, unconditional / label-conditional / signal-conditional; 'BioDiffusion')
papers.task: unconditional; class-cond; augmentation; also denoising, imputation, super-resolution
papers.datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (5-class beat version at 125 Hz); UniMiB SHAR (accelerometer); simulated shapes dataset
papers.loss_functions: Diffusion denoising loss with L1 norm (cosine noise schedule, 1000 steps)
papers.eval_metrics: Wavelet coherence; Discriminative score (2-layer LSTM real-vs-synthetic classifier error, TimeGAN-style); UMAP projections; visual inspection; downstream 1D-CNN per-class F1 / precision / recall on MIT-BIH with synthetic augmentation
papers.notes: Compared with C-RNN-GAN, RCWGAN, TimeGAN, SigCWGAN, TTS-GAN, TTS-CGAN. Wavelet coherence (0-1) between real and synthetic is unusual for ECG and captures time-varying spectral agreement. Diffusion loss uses L1 rather than L2.
papers.takeaway: Wavelet coherence and TimeGAN discriminative score are candidate additions to ECGEN-Eval.

papers.title: Personalized Heart Disease Detection via ECG Digital Twin Generation
papers.model_family: Hybrid (GAN + VQ: LAVQ-Editor with VQ-Separator / Disease Embedding Codebook, ClinicalBERT text guidance, AdaIN decoder, StyleGAN-like discriminator)
papers.task: text-cond / other (ECG editing: personalised 'digital twin' disease ECGs from a healthy patient ECG + reference disease ECG/report)
papers.datasets: PTB-XL (single-label superclasses; 291 test patients with both normal and disease ECGs)
papers.loss_functions: Generator: non-saturating logistic adversarial loss + L2 reconstruction + cosine disease-similarity loss + VQ loss; Discriminator: logistic adversarial loss + cosine disease-feature similarity loss
papers.eval_metrics: Fréchet ResNet Distance (FRD); ResNet Score (RS, Inception-Score analogue); k-NN precision, recall (Kynkäänniemi) and their F1; membership inference risk (F1 of distance-threshold attack in ResNet feature space, ε = τ·mean distance); patient-level personalised accuracy/F1 and Average Treatment Effect (ATE); ECG-level accuracy, F1, AUROC of 1D ResNet-34/GoogleNet; DTW to patient's real ECG (ablation); t-SNE of personal-information retention
papers.embedding_extractor: 1D ResNet-101 pretrained on PTB-XL training set (FRD, RS, precision/recall, MIA distances)
papers.notes: FRD real 0.30 vs ours 1.63 vs baselines 3.8-5.4; CGAN precision 0.997 but recall 0.069 — illustrates why precision alone misleads (mode collapse). MIA evaluated across thresholds τ. Compared CGAN, WGAN, StyleGAN, VQ-VAE2, PGANs.
papers.takeaway: Strong template: FD on an ECG-trained classifier + precision/recall/F1 + distance-threshold membership-inference curve; include a real-vs-real FD reference row.
